I feel compelled to write a review for Hob because I really loved it and I hope a lot of other people will try it and love it too.  If you've played Journey and felt moved by it, or have played a Zelda game and enjoy exploration, environmental puzzles and fluid combat then you're going to really have fun with Hob.  I've read many online reviews and the Metacritic scores just don't do it justice.  It's not a perfect game, but it really is fun and worth your time and money.
Hob is the kind of game that doesn't bore you with tutorials or backstory.  It plops you into its world and lets you explore.  The best way to play is to simply let your intuition and curiosity guide you.  The game does a great job of giving you waypoints so that if you get lost or bored exploring, you have a general sense of where to go and what to do next.  This game can be a very relaxed, zen-like experience, but there's enough mystery, puzzles and combat to keep things entertaining.  I personally feel you should just go where curiosity leads you and enjoy how solving puzzles transforms the landscape and opens up or changes the world.
As far as gameplay goes, Hob shines brightest with its fun environmental puzzles that unlock, change or move portions of the world around.  It's like the world itself is composed of this giant, living puzzle, and to progress, you figure out how to unlock it.  For the most part, the puzzles are fairly straightforward.  There were a few times that I spent maybe 10 minutes wondering exactly how I could get to a certain location, or how a puzzle worked.  Only once or twice did I almost check the Internet for help; but I didn't, and I'm glad I didn't have to.
The combat at first is a bit limited.  I kind of wish you could unlock some of the cooler elements earlier in the game so that everyone could enjoy teleporting through enemies and stunning them, or using the glove to knockback enemies.  When you combine the simplistic elements together you can actually create little combos and facing large groups becomes very enjoyable.  So my advice here is to upgrade your sword and your glove as soon as you can and don't forget to keep upgrading as you go.  Because it's not "necessary" it can be easy to forget, but it's well worth it.
Platforming is a little frustrating at times.  I feel like that's one area where the game could be improved.  The character sometimes feels "floaty" and not anchored to the world.  If they could get the physics of landing jumps and grabbing ledges the way the Tomb Raider games are able to, this game would be that much closer to perfect.  Even though you'll miss your share of jumps, it's by no means terrible and with all the well placed save points and lack of any real death penalty, it's no big deal anyway.
The world itself is incredibly beautiful and the art and level design group should be praised.  Animations are lovely.  Even ambient wildlife is beautifully animated and fun to watch and "pet".  I absolutely love that the developers allow you to pet animals.  I have wanted to do that in games since forever and it's a lovely touch.  Anyone who appreciates beautiful level design or who loves cell shaded style worlds should play this game just to appreciate how absolutely gorgeous it is.
The story in Hob is interesting and its mysteries are compelling enough to make you want to see how it all ends.  I enjoyed that there are multiple endings; although, it would've been nice to have a little more reason to choose between them.  In my opinion, there's not a compelling enough argument for one of them.  All that said, the story is somewhat light and I would've loved to have learned a bit more about some of this world's inhabitants and more of the backstory behind it; even if that was through pictograms or some other non-verbal method.
The game did feel a little short, but that said, I somehow managed to spend 30 hours playing it.  Yes, you can rush through it, but this is a game that you should just take your time and savor. I really hope that Runic adds some DLC to expand on those foggy gray areas on the upper left side of the map; and if not, I hope they consider making a sequel.  Games like Hob are some of my favorites and it feels like they only come along once in a while.  Thanks for your hard work team Runic!

I have played this game for years and still enjoy it. This is the steam version and I dont recommend this version of Teeworlds in particularily because other clients has far more features which enhance the gameplay.
Dummy Drag Race
The meat of the game is DDRace (dummy drag race). DDRace is where you play together with other players to finish a map, where you have to help each other. In these type of maps you take no damage from any weapon and they have been modified to aid you and your friend(s). In order to complete a map you need to have a friend with you otherwise it is impossible to make it on your own. Most maps starts with a 'noob-filter' which is kind of a warmup before the map starts the timer. After you complete the map the timer stops and you can track how long it took to finish it by holding TAB (default button). Some maps are easy to finish and some maps are hard which makes it hard for beginners/noobs to complete. This is also where you may have to make a choice...
Pros
- You can play with friends and also chose a team where you play and no other can interact, or just play with anybody
- There are tons of maps to play on
- controls are simple to learn
- More friendly players than not
- You can make your own maps (DDRace, CTF, DM, FNG, blockermaps etc.)
- Easy to setup server and community is big for q & a
- Light game ~ 30 Mb
- Colourful and cute
- no achievement pop-ups
Cons
- controls are hard to master
- steep learningcurve
- Trolls are everywhere these days and TW is no exception but you can vote to kick them (or join team)

- controls are sluggish and delayed (which makes you die hundreds of times and contributes to massive frustration and full metal rage quits), no matter if you are playing with M+K or controller
- dialogs look like they have been (mis-)translated from Chinese to English resulting in numerous spelling errors, weird grammar, or they just make no sense

Maybe if there were features like Double Jumps, Ledge Graps, Sprints, Weapon Upgrades, Usable Items and stuff like that the 'Metroidvania' tag would be justified, but in its current state I only see a pseudo game with great art style that basically lacks everything else.

I was really looking forward to this game, I loved the first game and played trough it multiple times. I had high hopes for this game, but it was a real disappointment.
The level design is awful, just awful. Theres nothing to write home about here, it's all ruined city after ruined city. Very few flashy locations like the first game. And traversing these new levels is a pain as well. Everything looks the same and has the same boring gray/brown color. You can very easily get lost and the only navigation help it gives you is a tiny white arrow that appears for a few seconds that you can only see if you are facing the right direction.
The game runs very poorly. It crashed very frequently and does not cooperate well with higher refresh rates. The game screen tears like crazy if you turn off V-sync, even if it is still within your monitor's natural refresh rate, and the game is not compatable with G-sync (I have yet to try Freesync, so I can't judge on that), so you still get the tearing. And if you turn on the games V-sync, it locks it to 60, which granted is not the wrost thing ever, but when I know my hardware can push 140, I would like to see 140. The only way I could fix it was to go to the Nvidia settings for the game and turn on Adaptive Sync. That seemed to clear up most of my issues.
The difficulty just seems ridiculous. Now a lot of people with just play this off as "Git Gud" but this is just absurd. You die far too quickly in the game, and it does not give you a good enough indication of where you are being shot from, nor a good indication that you are even being shot at all. Your screen just shakes oh so slightly when your hit, so you can lose a big chuck of health/armor before you even realise theres an enemy in the room.
I can't say this game is bad, but it is definitely a disappointment, everything good about it, the first game did better, so you might as well just play the first game. It had better gameplay, better levels, and runs without crashing all the time.

The game is VERY repetitive.
Throughout the entire game, each mission is pretty much the same.
- Travel to a city, where one of your targets are
- Talk to Assassin at bureau
- Complete 3 side activities (investigations) before you can take out your target
- Report back to Assassin at bureau
- Take out your target
- Run away and escape from guards
- Return to Assassin at bureau one last time to report success
- Return home to report of your success to Master
- Repeat (x9)
You have 9 targets total throughout the game, which means you do the SAME thing 9 times before the ending of the game.
It got to a point where I wasn't really playing for fun anymore, I was playing just to beat the game.
Nothing is really exciting about the game until the ending.
There is a major lack of story and personality with all the characters. You establish connections with NO ONE, because of all the missions being the same and there being a lack of build up or story behind those you are targeting.
No one is rememorable, except Warren, who I think had the MOST personality, and Altair of course, and even he lacks much of a personality, though he has more personality than anyone else in the game, except Warren.
People complain about Assassins like Connor lacking any personailty while Altair has almost NONE at all!
The little personality I got from Altair was; determined, focused, arrogant, and confused.
I suppose a better way of putting it was that he had lots of potential but what is given is performed horribly.
In later games there is story behind everyone you take out.
They wronged you, they serve a big role in the Templars, they have information, etc.
In this game, you get no story at all about anyone really, until the ending.
The combat isn't that good, with it being to just spam one button and hope whoever you're fighting doesn't reverse you randomly.
In later games combat is a little more fleshed out, with there being certain ways to fight certain enemies that make it more diverse, but here its the same fighting style over and over again, which adds to the repetitiveness of this game.
There isn't a diversity in enemies either, they're all the same, unless you want to count archers and swordsmen as 2 different enemies, but they fight the same.
Also I love (sarcasm) how when a sick guy pushes ME, it makes ME the criminal!

I haven't written a review in over a year, but this game got me to go ahead and write another one.
I went into this game blind, for the most part. The only things I knew were that this game was supposed to have a good story and a great soundtrack. I can already tell you that this game does deliver in both of these ways. The soundtrack is absolutely beautiful, and I will probably come back to it a lot just to listen to it. And I'm not usually one to listen to game soundtracks, really the only other two that I keep coming back to are Bastion and Undertale, and this game is certainly on eye level with those soundtracks.
I can't say much about the story without giving anything away, so I'm gonna be inentionally vague. The story was engaging throughout, had a lot of emotional moments (I cried more than once), and a lot of interesting turning points in the story. This one definitely stayed with me long after I finished the game.
That said, the game is also pretty short. It's about 4 hours total, with another hour or so from the free specials. I don't think it needs to be longer - it tells the story it wants to tell, and it feels right - but I personally don't like to stay with the same game too long so I might be biased in that way. I played the entire game in one session, and if you have the time I would consider doing the same, as it helps with keeping the athmosphere alive.
Overall, this was a great game, and I'm glad I purchased it bundled with the soundtrack. Thanks, past me (I bought it on sale half a year ago). I can recommend this game to everyone. If you like story-rich games, and don't mind it being a bit short, get it. You won't regret it. If you don't... well, I'd still recommend waiting for the next sale and picking it up for just a few bucks. You might find to like this game even if usually it's not your cup of tea.

Hob is the latest title from Runic Games, the developers of Torchlight 1 & 2. Set in a half organic, half machine world, it’s a wordless action/adventure game filled with exploration, light combat and mild puzzles. Drawing inspiration from titles such as Zelda, Ico and Shadow of Colossus (maybe even a bit of Metroid?), Hob takes things from each game and then adds its own spin on top of them while offering up a couple of new ideas in the process. After a friendly robot names Jeeves seemingly wakes you up to a partially deconstructed planet being taken over by an unknown life form, you start on a journey to get the world back to the way it was, all while finding out a bit more about what happened while you were slumbering.
After spending around 30 hours playing the game twice (average playtime seems to be around 10 hours) and spending almost another 35-40 (offline, so i wouldn't be forced to update) just running around exploring and taking screenshots, i can safely say Hob has become one of my favorite games of all time. Even after spending all those hours getting to know the game world pretty thoroughly, i still crave more. While playing, and even afterwards, the feeling of one more thing waiting to be discovered was always present. And i don’t just mean normal gameplay type things (like a new upgrade, story revelations or a brand new area), i also mean things like little spots on the map you haven’t made it to yet, or maybe new paths to objectives you never realized were right in front of you. And this, to me, is why Hob is such a special game. The world, and the characters that inhabit it, are so full of detail, mystery and charm, you can’t help but want to explore and experience every last thing the game has to offer, big or small. Runic Games has utterly succeeded in creating an unique, intriguing and atmospheric world that just begs to be discovered. I never got tired of trying to reach a new vantage point just to take in the beautiful views or scouring the different areas looking for the subtle environmental storytelling.
I found Hob to be a great mix of exploring, puzzles, combat and platforming. The level design is amazing, always keeping things fresh and interesting. The way the world moves and shifts as you complete objectives is so satisfying. Even small things, like creating steps out of the side of a wall, are moments of joy. The puzzles aren’t difficult yet they offer a light challenge and a nice change of pace. The combat, while simple, is enjoyable and gets even better once you unlock some of your upgrades (the charge/ground punch that blows apart enemies is especially gratifying). A few of these upgrades also enhance your movement, making traveling around the planet easier, quicker and all around more fun. The platforming can also be quite engaging (and even intense at times), however the fixed camera angle (it’s mostly from a top down perspective) got me killed on a few occasions. This is one of the two things i would change about the game if i could. The ability to have a camera i could control would be priceless. Not only for gameplay reasons, but also so i could view this gorgeous game from different perspectives. I almost feel the fixed camera does the game a disservice by limiting what you can see of it, and i desperately want to see it all! Even a first person look around mode would be hugely appreciated. While i can understand one of the reasons for it (to make the player feel small and world feel big) it comes at the cost of a bit of mystery, since you know what’s around almost every corner before you get there. The other thing i would change is the fall damage. It’s a bit too restricting in my opinion, especially for a game that wants you to explore and has lots of potentially fun cliffs you could jump off of.
Visually, the game is a dazzler. I fell in love with the art style the very first time i saw it and love it even more now after completing the game. The attractive colors, the way the cloud shadows roll across the ground, the gently blowing grass that realistically moves as you walk through it. These all help pull you into the world of Hob. Throw in top notch animation, tons of passionately crafted details (like all the animals that help make the world feel alive, the tiny sprite creatures who watch you curiously, and the wavy wind gusts that streak across the screen) and add a moody and relaxing soundtrack and you get quite a magical experience.
I did run into a few glitches during my playthroughs (like falling through a few walls and disappearing water), but nothing too bad. The developers have been hard at work listening to feedback and constantly patching the game though, so i’m confident most/all of the bugs will be ironed out quickly, if they haven’t been fixed already.
At $20 Hob is a steal. The fun and quality you get for that price is crazy. I think they could have asked $30-35 easily and that would have been more than fair. But at the same time, i’m glad they set it at a lower price point if that means more people are able to experience this wonderful title. It definitely exceeded all my expectations and i hope and pray one day we’ll get another game set in the brilliant world of Hob. Highly highly recommend.
Huge thanks to Runic Games for the review copy.

This game is pretty damn awesome.
If you like metal, gothic pixel art and frustratingly hard bullsh*t like old Castlevania or Ghosts'n'Goblins, this is a game for you. The soundtrack, the aesthetics, the atmosphere...it's all close to perfect. I'd actually say this is a spiritual successor to the NES metal tribute game Holy Diver, which is a similar level of badassery but was sadly limited by the possibilities of the NES.
Now, I'd only have one criticism of this game - which is a big one though: it needs customisable controls.
The keyboard controls just don't feel intuitive to me (and I realise this was designed for a gamepad, but I'm just more used to playing on keyboard). At the very least, there should be a menu option to show a basic explanation of the controls, I've died a bunch of times before I actually figured out how to do the super move.
I've also seen a lot of people complain that the controls are slow and unresponsive, but I personally think that's an artistic choice. This game is supposed to be a tribute to old games like Castlevania and Ghosts'n'Goblins, and those also have similarly slow controls - I have such fond childhood memories of raging over the sluggish controls in The Castlevania Adventure on gameboy, I'm used to this by now. It's not intolerably slow, so it passes imo.
I'd recommend this because the developer said they'd fix the controls, so I'll hope that my problems with the game will be gone in the future. If they are, this gets a full 10/10 from me.

Definitely one of my games of the year. Here are some highlights:
Audio
A pair of headphones - use them! Hellblade has audio recorded with special kind of microphones. This enables you to pinpoint the exact direction and distance of the sounds. In practice, some sounds now have a sort of "presence" added to them (think about regular monitor vs VR goggles). Very refreshing.
Narrative
The player character has many voices in her head. Their constant chatter is something where the audio design really shines. The voices talk about very different things. Sometimes they advice you, taunt you, judge you, try to manipulate you or reveal bits of information. Boy, does it build up the immersion. Sense of immediate danger, desperation, insecurity. I bet this is the best depiction of mental illness in a video game so far. In addition, there are some flashbacks to shed more light on the backstory.
Combat
Has some nice touches and can be enjoyable, but is pretty basic after all. Sadly, it soon become repetitive and seemed to last way too long. That might be due to having the adaptive difficulty enabled. The game is not about combat really and it is not too off-putting to enjoy the game.

I am only a couple hours into the game so take that into consideration when reading this.  I also won't be singing all it's praises cause  there are already plenty of reviews doing that and they are all well justified.  The game is beautiful, especially on a 4k big screen.  Narative is solid and the story good enough to keep you engaged.
Combat:  A  little clunky but once you get used to the timing it is not as bad as some would say and I find it quite rewarding to pull off some harder to make combos because of that.  The combat animations are also pretty enjoyable to watch.
Choices:  So far there are none,   You basically just follow the narative and listen to the voices in your head.  There is also no npc interaction because, well, there are no NPCs to interact with.  If you are looking for some meaningful dialogue you won't find it here.
Exploration:  About as much as "Choices".  There is no road less traveled.
Puzzles:  So far, quite simple really.  Not a lot of head scratching required but it works well enough to not slow the pacing of the game.  It really is about the story and quite frankly I and happy to not have it get bogged down by puzzles and extra tasks.
All in all, I am loving it.  Dispite some shortcomings Hellfire does one thing extremely well and that is tell a story and Senua is probably the most interesting character I have had the pleasure of getting to know.  If you are looking for a good story to get lost in then I highly recommend you play this game.

TribeQuest: Red Killer is yet another mobile port to hit the Steam storefront. After the game had no reviews for nearly a week I decided to just drop the .99 and give it a try. The first major thing to note is that the game in the trailer is a much older version of the game (3 years old), and the game in the screenshots (that work) is a more accurate representation.
Red Killer is, unfortunately, currently just another poor mobile port. The physics in the levels are somewhat broken and things will be left in positions that should be impossible. The English is also lackluster, with the game featuring a lot of missing punctuation and some misspelled words. There's also poor hints as to what you're actually supposed to do when you start the game outside of the game being called "Red Killer". There's no in-game options, the "pause" button doesn't actually pause the game, and the quit button doesn't actually work. The game is also not properly widescreen, and if you play at any sort of widescreen resolution you will be stuck with bars on the side.
Until the physics can get massively cleaned up I suggest avoiding this. To the developer, I suggest trying to actually make this game look like it belongs on Steam/PC and not make it be just another bad mobile port. I also suggest cleaning up the presentation of the game on the store page - get an updated trailer that isn't just failing at levels over and over. Make all of the screenshots actually work and have them be something that would work to sell the game.

OK So for starters I haven't beaten the game, original or Deathinitive. I got the franchise pack on sale earlier this year. I was pleasantly surprised today that the Deathinitive edition was coming to PC already, let alone that I got it free (yes I know that some people who got the steam version and the DLC for it did not get it free and that sucks, like, really sucks), but I noticed that the game has a lot of negative reviews on steam, mostly for framerate issues and crashes upon loading a save.
For starters, the crashing upon loading a save is due to issues with maxed out shadows. I don't know why this happens but you can easily turn it down a notch in the old Darksiders II and it should work (it did for me). If you don't have the original version and you max out shadows I'm certain there's a way to edit options.dopt to fix it. The shadow quality is still much higher than the blocky shadow textures in the original version regardless.
Another issue I came across was that the resolution was much higher than it was supposed to be. and since my resolution before was 3840x2160 it resulted in me only being able to see a quarter of the screen. I set the game to 1080p fullscreen before switching back and it worked fine after that. Not sure which of the 2 fixed it though.
As for framerate issues (note that I only tested in the City of the Dead, it's where my save file was when the Deathinitive edition released) I have a GTX 980 running the game at 3840x2160 windowed (forced borderless) with second highest shadow quality, no anti aliasing, and anistrophic filtering on. My framerate didn't drop below 50 during gameplay. That's not great for a game with limited graphics options but you can lower other things. This may just be my graphics card and it may be a serious plague to people with less powerful GPU's (even at 1920x1080) but I can't say for certain.
As far as improvements go it's mostly graphical (although I do like the graphical improvements quite a bit) but I feel like the aiming controls with a controller improved a lot. Before if I did light flicks to position my cursor precisely every 3rd flick would send the cursor flying, screwing up my aim. Fortunately that is no longer an issue. And I don't know if this is typical for remasters of PC games (on PC) but my save file did carry over to the deathinitive edition, which was a nice surprise for me. And of course the game is still very solid on it's own merits. Not the greatest PC port, or PC remaster but it's servicable and the game itself is great. If nothing else it's a better PC port than the one the first Darksiders got.

After playing this game to death on Desura, before the Steam release, I somewhat forgot about it, despite thoroughly enjoying it. Was very pleased to see it's seen continued development and a Steam release.
The game's a fairly casual, top down shooter, with relatively hardcore mechanics. Think of it as Arma Lite. Bullets are deadly, explosive and vehicles are deadlier. Tactics and coordination are a must in order to advance. Squad mechanics work well, and the AI is competent and deadly, indeed. There's a wide variety of weapons and vehicles to utilise, including rifles, LMGs, shotguns, explosives and APCs, as well as a handfull of fun gamemodes, as well as mod support.
I hope the multiplayer community grows further, as I feel this game could really shine as a nice pick-up and play squad based shooter.
Graphics and sound are good, whilst 'basic'. The style is reminiscent of good old green army men toys. Particle effects like explosions and muzzle flair are nice, and punch up the 'toy' style.
Overall if you want a fun top-down to jump into every once in a while, but still enjoy some of the depth you'd get from it's bigger cousins, this game is a must.

I'm conflicted, I would like to say this game is great and everyone should buy it. However, on a 1 to 10 scale I would honestly have to give it a 5.5, but no higher then a 6.
From my history of playing this games series, what really sucked me in back in 2008 (ish, I don't exactly recall the date) was from an Assassin's Creed YouTube trailer featuring "Lonely Soul" by Unkle. So there's Altair walking down an empty street in what looks to be the lone swordsman routine when, Bam, out pops an ten inch hidden blade. Yeah, there were other trailers like the one where he storms a hanging with a crossbow, but the song did it for me.
So, I bought it, and, then as I do now, I still hate the game. And I still love the game.
HUH?
Let me explain...
- I felt like it never got to use the hidden blade as much as I would like to.
- He never go to use a crossbow. It almost felt like a like, but whatever.
- He will smack into walls as if he was drunk... constantly. I spent days shouting, "What are you?...I didn't want to go that way? Why did you jump off that building? Did you have to kill another random person? WTF you can't swim?!!"
- He can't swim. Yes, the master assassin will drown in the shallow end of the kiddie pool, floaties and all.
- The first 40 minutes are hell. In fact, I almost gave up just from the droll that pored from Lucy, Desmond and the Dr.
- The game could have stood alone with out a the cutscenes with Desmond. And Ubi wisely turned some of those 'inner' scenes into missions that were more fun later on.
- You're required to learn almost every new move he's given, which also slows down the game.
- You will hate the hordes of NPC's running between you and the combat.
So, why even play it?

- Boredom. Seriously.
- It has a unique storyline.
- I actually contemplated some of the philosophy.
- Altair is a one-shot wonder with his throwing knives. He will kill almost anyone with one blade, too bad I can't say the same later in the series.
- Sometimes when he turns the wrong way or runs off ledges, it's comical. And frustrating.
- Stealing throwing knives is easier then buying them.
- No monetary system, this is both good and bad, but in this game it worked.
- The ending is was worth the wait.

Have you ever had that dream where you're being chased by someone?  Well, now you can play that dream!  This is a game about running, climbing, jumping, being chased, hiding, and then finally you realize the truth - it's just way faster to stop and kill everyone chasing you than it is to run away in the first place.  I'm not exactly sure if this is what the creaters intended, but it's cathartic all the same.  All the same, this is a fun little game with a pretty-good plot (you won't really care about any of the characters, and the main character is only kinda interesting...his artificial arc definitely isn't going to leave you on the edge of your seat...so just get back to the stabbing).  As a "stealth" game, it comes a little short because it really isn't that except for the fact that you do kinda surprise people by suddenly stabbing them, then walking away (spoiler alert!).  (I mean, that would be surprising unless you live in like New York or Chicago or Detroit or LA where you kinda expect random people to do this.)  As a console port, the controlls are hillariously wonky to the point of comedy, when your character alternates being being a master acrobat to being the most clumsy creature in the world, seemingly at random.  The fighting is pretty much the same.  This game does have some silly camera tricks, though it (generally) sometimes avoids annoying angles, unless you are fighting.  It has automatic checkpoints, but the saving isn't really a big deal, and it tends to save every time you need it to.  This isn't a difficult game, at all, but I think it's supposed to be all about the ride.  It CTDs very rarely, but it's nothing to worry about.  Overall, it's a better than average ride, all things considered.  Oh, yeah, I got all the flags and templars, which takes like a million hours, and do you know you get exactly NOTHING for so doing.  Oh, yeah, ignore the flags and templars, unless you hate yourself :|

I will admit, I was hyped for this game. I wanted to explore the stars with my friends, become a space pirate, and buy huge ships to engage in explosive space battles.
Safe to say, my expectations were shattered to say the least.
After the initial backlash and lack of communication from the developers, I thought that I would never purchase the game. Then the updates came, peaking my interest again. I finally took the plunge.
+ Tutorial was good. Explained the basics of the game.
+ Planets and fauna are varied.
+ Weather system can make the game interesting, e.g. acid rain.
+ Base building is slowly becoming more interesting.
+ Basic multiplayer finally introduced.
+ Game looks gorgeous.
+ Camera mode.
+ Resources to power ships are easily scavengeable.
+ Can add interesting mods to your mining laser.
+ Different ways to play. Some more viable than others.
+ Uploading discoveries for others to see.
+ Enjoy slowly learning the alien languages.
- The cave systems are pointless. You never find decent loot, it's ridiculously easy to get lost in them, and they all generally look the same.
- Ships run out of rersources incredibly quickly. While the resources are quite easy to locate, it gets tedious having to go mining every few landings.
- The economy system is bad. If you dont farm a few certain items, you are not going to flourish in this game.
- New ships are expensive. Like really expensive. I've played 20 hours so far and made about 3 million credits. Half decent ships can be around 300 million. Really not realistic.
- No tutorial about making credits, other than mining and selling what you mine.
- Ship combat is a bit dodgy at times. AI never misses and will gang up on you to destroy you quickly. As previously stated, you can't afford to buy a new ship to combat this threat. Dont make many credits doing this unless you target the huge armadas.
- Sentinels. I bought this game to explore, not to get ambushed by annoying little robots if I decide to mine something on every planet.
- Missions are usually fetch quests, or go ans scan something and come back.
- Combat is meh.
- Proper multiplayer still not implimented. Other players appear as glowing orbs. Cant really interact.
- Planets start to look the same after a while.
- Hyperdrive fuel. I want to explore planets, not go mining for ages if I want to explore somewhere different.
- "Your inventory is full"
The thing about No Man's Sky is that it has huge potential, and thats what annoys me. It's so close to being a really good game but its just not there yet. You can feel that it's unfinished as you play it.
Many of the core gameplay features are flawed but with some work, I do believe that No Man's Sky could be the game that we all wanted originally. I truly hope that the developers keep working at this game, as it could be something special in the future, but as of right now, I can't recommend it.

After the onslaught of bad reviews and a historically terrible launch, I'm amazed I'm giving this game a good review.
I got into this game about 6 months before release and I was extremely disappointed in what was released. I followed along as the developers added base-building and a few other core aspects to the game but it wasn't enough for me to get into it. When I saw the recent Atlas Rises update and the $24 sale price tag, I had to try it out.
I was not disappointed at all, in fact, I can't put this game down. It has been a long time since a game has gripped me like this. This game used to be defined as "As wide as an ocean but as deep as a puddle." I think the developers have completely fixed this aspect. There's a lot of depth to this game. I usually start playing with a goal in mind, but I find myself exploring or doing something different for hours on end. For instance, I may be traveling to a different system for a mission, then spot a downed ship. I, then, will spend 30 minutes to an hour fixing it up and claiming it as my own.
I will say there are still some cons. The core of the game is very grindy. You have to grind resources or trade for Units to get anything done. The other con would have to be with procedural generation, as a whole. With games like these, you start to see the same bases, plants, animals, scenarios repeated on different planets. If you've played a game like Starbound, you know how that feels. After a while, I'm sure I'll run out of things to do and it will just be a game of hopping from system to system to beat the main goal. I would have also liked to see multiplayer. I know the developers seem to be moving in that direction, but it would really make this game a true masterpiece.
For all of those reasons, I would also say, I wouldn't spend more than $30 on this game. Wait until it goes on sale.
I would also say that if you want a fast-paced game with clear goals and objectives, do not buy this game. Beyond that, if you like open-world, exploration, survival space sims, this is the one you need to get.

Early Kickstarter backer and shower-offer-to-friends-er, with rather hurt feelings about it all
During development, update-after-update showed new sprites or boasted new music but rarely if ever info on combat, gameplay, enemy AI.
That fact says it all.
Cringing from the writing (which is so bad it seems like an active attempt to *sabotage* the game), even before I got to experience the extremely painful controls and terrible combat.
Music is really cool for a few minutes but 30 mins in, it was getting very very repetitive.
== And the long rant version of this review: ==
The controls are fundamentally painful. You have to hold a button down for about a second just to turn around, due to mistakenly implemented analog sensitivity in Unity even when using a keyboard. Attack combos are an inconsistent mish-mash. I think that duck is the same as block but you're better off trying to bash the attack button since blocking only works on projectiles--meaning if fighting melee & ranged opponents simultaneously, blocking gets you killed.
After pressing every key on my keyboard I found a cool looking fireball which was semi-useful.
Earn mana by using 'decapitate' button (W key--you're welcome) but it only works on enemies with very low HP, and it's slow and short-ranged and leaves you vulnerable. It seems to me to be essentially useless since you can't gauge enemy HP (unless you count the hits you've made and know how many it takes, but that's nearly impossible when fihgting 2-3 at once). Even if one of the enemies in a group is low enough, using decap means you'll almost certainly be hit 1-2x by the other guys.
Attempting to hit an enemy and then run or run and turn around and attack again is entirely futile, due to the terrible turn-around speed and very very clunky controls. The dodge key itself didn't prove useful enough to bother with due to the clunkiness (approach enemy, attack, dodge--you're likely to be hit before your attack finishes and the dodge executes).
Fortunately, I was able to dispatch groups of enemies by simply standing on a raised ledge, watching them walk endlessly into it, and attacking them whilst crouching. Take that, mindless undead!
My general feeling about the combat was that MAYBE it would be possible to game it perfectly and get past enemies by maintaining a specific distance, attacking, dodging backward, attacking again but I'm no slouch and after many many lives lost, found it nearly impossible to defeat groups without sustaining damage.
I got so frustrated by the controls after what what was probably my 20th attempt at getting past a section leading up to the "red skelly" right after entering the 1st temple that I closed the game so can't comment any further.
I'll try to check back after some patches have been released in a month or two, and hopefully get a bit further and be able to write a nicer review.

The trailer and screenshots absolutely do an injustice to this masterpiece. Never have I witnessed a work of art as entertaining as this video game. The plot is an emotional rollercoaster from beginning to end. Without spoiling any important plot points, you play as an ex-rock paper scissors champion who has fallen from glory. After winning countless championships, the champ feels hollow on the inside, resorting to fruitiously spending his victory money on high-class drugs and expensive alcohol. The champ falls further and further down the hole known as substance abuse until eventually, our hero loses his wife and two children in a car accident. The champ feels truly worthless at this point, quitting rock paper scissors tournaments and losing his home. Homeless, wifeless, childless, and broken, the champ decides to enlist in the military. After a four year term in the middle-east, the champ learns first-hand the atrocities of war. Ashamed of the horrors he committed by the orders of his commanding officer, the champ comes back to America to rekindle his relationship with the last thing he holds dear to his heart, rock paper scissors. The champ must face opposition and hardships no man before him has faced, all in the name of rock paper scissors. It is time for the champ to reclaim his throne. Truly a diamond in the ruff. 10/10, a masterpiece.

text:
is a very touching story about two doctors entering a dying patient's memory and fulfilling his wish for life. When I finished the game at midnight, my eyes were watery.
The game itself isn't long. You are bound to finish after around 4 hours, including the 2 minisodes as sort of an after story. The game still tells a complete story with a clear story line.
The following are thoughts on the story, PLEASE READ AFTER FINISHNIG THE GAME.
The story isn't what would qualify as a classic; but nonetheless, it is interesting enough, and it is good enough to get you to tears.
The game is humorous at times, sometimes creepy, and sad and touching sometimes. The game manages a good balance among all the emotional elements.
Even though the game allows free movement and interaction, the game should fall into the category of visual novels.
I almost forgot to mention, the game features very good soundtracks. The touching plot would never be complete without the help of the OST. For a 4-hour-game, there are 33 songs (around an hour in total), and this is quite impressive.
Some Cons:
-Sometimes walk too slowly
-The background is sometimes too messy (took me a while to find the rabbit in a stage)
-Some obstacles on the map makes poor gameplay
Improvements:
-Puzzles could be more complex
-Stories could be more complex, with multiple endings even
The shortcomings does not overcome the shining points of this game. Even though it is not as impressive as some claim, The story is still worth experiencing. To me, the metacritic score of 81/100 fits this game pretty good. The steam review of 97% positive reviews is a bit bloated. Steam needs a middle ground for reviewing.

This is a remastered version of one of my favorite games and franchises, Darksiders II. The Deathinitive Edition offers an additional difficulty level, improved visuals (especially lighting), and rebalanced loot and enemies.
If you've already played Darksiders II before, it's the same game you know and love but prettier. If you've never played Darksiders II, it's a wild ride and a very challenging experience. The combat is visceral and the controls tight and responsive. There are some minor camera issues but you'll learn to adjust to the controls (gamepad highly recommended).
Players new to the series should start with and beat Darksiders I first, before moving onto this title, to get the full breadth of the detailed and winding story. The Darksiders franchise offers a lot to love, from the art and music direction to the weapon skills and enemies. Darksiders II picks up the torch and never slips up.
This is one game (franchise) I highly recommend. This remaster in particular is 100% faithful to the original and definitely a good bit harder and prettier.

This is a tough one to talk about.
I was drawn to Remember me because I played Life is strange, fell in love with it and then had a more in depth look at the developers of that game (Dontnod) and in doing so came across this. There are plenty of ways the games are similar but they're very far from being a similar experience so don't come looking for a Life is strange fix.
It's tough to talk about because I had a somewhat hard time getting into this game (multiple attempts) and then a somewhat non-enthusiast time getting through it. Yet at the same time there are a lot of aspects I want to praise first:
+Great story (really comes into its own only at the end parts though)
+Beautiful graphics
+Well made world with its version of the future and lore
+Surprisingly good combat system (one of the things that kept me coming back for more actually)
+Good voice acting and animations
So what was my problem?
-The environments feel constricting and navigating them can be a bit awkward (You're teased with being Ezio Auditore whilst trapped in a highly linear environment and narrative)
-A bunch of story elements seemed to me debatable and dubious
-Whilst the story and world are well made, the environments also manage to largely feel grey and the majority of them are not memorable
Those points and then there's the bit how collectibles are really hard to find... Really the negatives are more like subjective barriers that kept me from fully enjoying the positives rather than an entire side of the game. They could also be a result of me trying to compare Remember me to other games I've liked too hard and so having specific expectations.
All in all there's definitely something to this one. It's fairly short so give it a chance

This could have been one of my all-time favorites. Great soundtrack. Amazing atmosphere. It has a Tomb Raider type feel for traversing certain areas - with hacking locks and moving objects in order to progress. You get to see memories via other characters, find hidden items, and learn more about the protagonist as you go. If this had been a bigger portion of the game it would have been a winner (and at first it was...)
Now the downfalls.
Once you go through certain doors (none of which are indicated) you can’t go back. The fact that you can’t explore is discouraging. Miss that hidden item? Oh, well. Also, if you die before the next auto-save any hidden items you did find revert back. Which will happen because the camera angles are odd and sometimes you jump to your death. Some of these items offer stat boosts.
The combat is a combo fight style. For the first half of the game fights are engaging but not overly difficult or long. The boss fights were fun. One boss. Right move/dodge at the right time. Then half-way through it becomes a sh*t storm of enemies...and more enemies...and more enemies...over and over. You can’t fully use your combos at this point because there are too many swarming you. The fights overtake the game and become tiresome and a hassle.
This brings me to the next issue that killed the game for me. This has some of the worst boss fights I’ve ever encountered. Some are nothing but waiting on two-minute cool-downs and avoiding attacks. Others are long drawn out button mashing torture sessions. One fight was so bad I swore I would never do another boss fight like that again. Twenty minutes later I’m fighting TWO OF THEM and their horde of zombie type enemies swarming me non-stop. My controller nearly took a rage fueled trip across the room.
Since the combat is a major portion of the game I can't recommend unless on sale. A well-developed game should not be so frustrating. There was clearly a lot of ambition, but it feels like they lost focus on what they were trying to create half-way through.

After the onslaught of bad reviews and a historically terrible launch, I'm amazed I'm giving this game a good review.
I got into this game about 6 months before release and I was extremely disappointed in what was released. I followed along as the developers added base-building and a few other core aspects to the game but it wasn't enough for me to get into it. When I saw the recent Atlas Rises update and the $24 sale price tag, I had to try it out.
I was not disappointed at all, in fact, I can't put this game down. It has been a long time since a game has gripped me like this. This game used to be defined as "As wide as an ocean but as deep as a puddle." I think the developers have completely fixed this aspect. There's a lot of depth to this game. I usually start playing with a goal in mind, but I find myself exploring or doing something different for hours on end. For instance, I may be traveling to a different system for a mission, then spot a downed ship. I, then, will spend 30 minutes to an hour fixing it up and claiming it as my own.
I will say there are still some cons. The core of the game is very grindy. You have to grind resources or trade for Units to get anything done. The other con would have to be with procedural generation, as a whole. With games like these, you start to see the same bases, plants, animals, scenarios repeated on different planets. If you've played a game like Starbound, you know how that feels. After a while, I'm sure I'll run out of things to do and it will just be a game of hopping from system to system to beat the main goal. I would have also liked to see multiplayer. I know the developers seem to be moving in that direction, but it would really make this game a true masterpiece.
For all of those reasons, I would also say, I wouldn't spend more than $30 on this game. Wait until it goes on sale.
I would also say that if you want a fast-paced game with clear goals and objectives, do not buy this game. Beyond that, if you like open-world, exploration, survival space sims, this is the one you need to get.

The gameplay... sort of sucks? There are a lot of extremely frustrating elements that got ironed out of future games. Walking in a group requires constant button pressing to lock you in place, deviating from that cover at all will immediately make guards hostile in many parts of the game world. This can be incredibly frustrating in the more open areas where you'd rather move quickly. And in crowds where you have to stay hidden, combined with 'crazy' npcs that will shove you which registers as your cover being blown and the guards descending en-masse... well it is controller-chucking levels of maddening at times.
The camera sucks. This game has no cinematography beyond the occasional opportunity to switch fixed camera angles (which has to be done manually at specific times for some reason). This is a problem games have in general, interesting voice overs but nothing happening visually. It's very dull even if you like what your ears are hearing. Like watching a CCTV video of a conversation in the middle ages. I spent what felt like genuine hours of the game making Altair do pirouettes by tapping left and right rhythmically.
This game had a flow and purity later games lacked in my opinion. It also had a focus on the philosophical ramifications of its story as well that the sequels had no interest in whatsoever. While the future sections were tedious and entirely prefunctory the main meat of the story was very enjoyable. There was a strong focus on what exactly the Assassin's creed  meant, which was parallelled with Altair's character arc and his evolving relationship with a couple of key characters. The actual assasinations held thematic weight too, with the game exploring each of the target's sins eventually cumulating with a monologue from the villains as they lie dying in your arms (a mechanic future games have, but without the meaningful exposition being given by the characters) offering their side of the story and their justification for their actions, lending a final human touch to them.
It also hinges a final plot twist on something that initially felt like it was going to be a "Wait, didn't they just?" Chekhov's Gun that I genuinely expected the writers to have been ignorant of including, so it was a pleasant surprise that yet another video game plot hole was actually an intentional twist.
The soundtrack by Jesper Kyd is as solid as to be expected. It has a modern, electronic, style that later games wisely ditched (along with Altair's inexplicable American accent), but I confess to really liking it still. Particularly the pulse pounding track that plays after a successful assassination as you run from the authorities and attempt to regain anonymity, it gave every sequence a moment of "
".
Also, as anyone who has played the later games already knows, the controller prompts for the PC version are absolutely bewildering at first with you constantly trying to work out which is the 'feet' button.
Its a shame there's such strongly frustrating elements in this game as I feel like in some ways it is also the best Assassin's Creed, before the plot became empty hollywood blockbuster fluff and the gameplay became a sequence of distractions and "stay exactly 30 feet behind this NPC without breaking line of sight for about 15 minutes" missions.

Slain Expectations
Full disclosure: review copy provided by developer/publisher!
And so like The Lady before it, Steam has sharted out another half-baked indie title for us to enjoy in the waning days of winter – this time it's Slain!, an arcadey, 2D hack n' slash. Let me get this out of the way right off the bat: this isn't an AWFUL game. It looks great... no, it looks SPECTACULAR. This is lovingly crafted stuff: the baddies, the bosses, the backgrounds, the foregrounds, the GROUNDgrounds! It's a slick looking, heavy metal album cover of a game.
But it all falls apart, unfortunately, like a conversation with a beautiful airhead.
“So what kind of hobbies do you have, Slain!?”
“Pizza!”
“Pizza isn't a hobby, Slain.”
“Horses!”
“Alright, we're done here.”
It's just kind of... vapid? That's my biggest complaint, and the most damning, unpatchable one. The combat has no impact... and that's CRITICAL for a hack n' slash. What it lacks in combat depth it should make up for in VIOLENT, RADICAL, FEEL-GOOD COMBAT. It doesn't sound good, and it doesn't feel good. The majority of the game you can spam the attack button and watch as the minions of SATAN crumble like so much tissue paper before your standard sword.  Hell, I didn't realize I could switch between elemental weapons or use spirit bombs until halfway through the game (I figured they mentioned fire, ice, and steel as a Game of Thrones reference or something, honestly). I guess that's another issue in and of itself: the game doesn't really explain itself well. “Spirit bombs are great for clearing out tons of enemies!” Thanks game! How in the ♥♥♥♥ do I do that?
And besides all that you run along a fairly linear path, slapping switches and jumping on platforms. It's all very uninspired, save for the brilliant art design. And the story? Forgettable. You play as one Geralt - I mean Bathoryn? And you have been brought back to life to destroy evil? And that's that. Go around and kill evil. And the dialogue is bizarrely disjointed - sometimes they stick to the old timey spiel, sometimes there's a weird modern tone that's just short of "LOL."
This is likely a byproduct of this game having been rushed out the door before it was ready... it was delayed at least twice as far as I know, and it still feels unrefined, unpolished, unfinished. The platforming is MOSTLY okay, but there are some serious spatial issues with some platforms (lookin' at you Wolfswood Caves with your stupid aggravating smashy, insta-death falls if you don't jump on the last frickin' pixel of a GOD DAMN LEDGE ♥♥♥♥). The enemies all look cool, but they're just so much fodder – even the bosses. Slash 'em, run around 'em, slash 'em, rinse and repeat, dead. I seldom had to dodge, just casually smack them as they (in futility) try and break through my attack spamming.
Despite there being checkpoints, if you quit out of the game during a level you have to start the whole damned thing over again – and some of the more frustrating, platformy ones can take a substantial amount of time. If you decide you have somewhere else to be don't quit out until you actually beat the damned boss. Once you beat an area you're free to explore, replay a level... but why would you? It's mostly linear, the combat is unsatisfying, and the “puzzles” aren't all that puzzley.
At the end of the day this is a gussied up pig. It looks AMAZING – but wipe away the makeup and you'll see it's a Berkshire boar with beady little soulless eyes. Even if they fix the myriad of issues (achievements, control issues, sound issues, typos) this is one to avoid unless heavily discounted.

A better review of the game. (This might be a tad bit arrogent)
So I like this game and here is why:
1. I like the difficulty with the game
2. I like the old school feel to it
3. There is a learning curve to the game and it rewards you for learning
So lets delve into this:
A. Graphics
B. Game Play
C. Music
D. Controls
Graphics:
Excellent graphics. It brings back memories of Ghost and Gobblins and the 8 bit era. Very metal, very metal. The only complaint is that some of the traps blend in very easily into the environment, although that may be the intent of the developers.
Game Play:
You have access to quite a few things that make the game interesting. To discover them is part of the game, and the game was meant to relive some of the old style hype. So if you discover the flame sword fairly early on and then die, then can you re-equip it? or is it gone forever? (HINT: LOOK AT THE CONTROL SECTION). You have access to three primary attacks with one screen wipe: Regular slash, beheading slash, range magic attack, and magic bomb. With the other two unlock weapons or so, you get different effects with each of the slashes. For example, the flame sword is faster and moves you further across the screen, while the ice axe will throw enemies quite a distance from you.
There is an indicator for everything, but you would have to figure out what it means, and I will make a beginners guide on what each one means. For example, why do enemies have a red line around their necks? or why is there blood all over that patch of ground that the surrounding area lacks?
Each enemy has a clear pattern and a clear counter play to them and some have counter play to alternative attacks. (HINT: DO NOT BOMB THE BIG RED SKELETONS) so the frustation there is that the patterns will change as you unlock more weapons. But I like a game that evolves with you.
Music:
I like the chords that are playing in the background. Yeah the repeat every so often, and so times they cover up sound clues to what you need to do next. Aside from that, you can control the music from the pause menu. If you don't like metal chords, then play with no sound.
Controls:
This seems to be the biggest complaint of the game. However, I disagree with those complaints. Before the game loads, a white box shows up and you can change the controls from there. The controls are as follows for those that do not have a joy stick or game pad:
arrow keys for move left, move right, jump and block (which is down)
Q for quick slash
W for beheading slash
1 for range magic attack
2 for normal sword
3 for flame sword
4 for ice axe
p for pause
enter for continue or navigating the menu's
Now for some of that good old explaination for how the controls work:
Your momentum is controlled by a few things: how long you are holding the key, and whether or not you have taken damage. Damage stops your momentum, so a couple of parts are hard because of a range enemy on the other side of a pit. That was fun to figure out.
The platforms that are solid are solid through and through. That means if you try to jump to another platform from underneath, you will bonk your head and lose some of your momentum.
Each weapon has a plus and a minus to how it works:
Normal weapon is a basic no bonus and no minus tool. The downside is that other weapons will handle situations better and you will take damage from enemies, because this things has a very small stun lock.
Range magic is good for dealing with weak enemies that you are having some trouble reaching. It consumes a small amount of mana, but with a full bar you can maybe fire it off about 10 times.
Flame sword is good agains witches. It is faster and deals less damage, while moving you farther with each attack.
Ice axe is good against most creatures, but terrible against witches. Each swing has a big stun time and the final swing in a normal combo knocks an enemy back far enough for you to reset and move.
TLDR:
The game's difficulty comes from not giving you any sort of tutorial to learn anything. It expects you to 1. be patient and not click, click through the game. 2. pay attention and try different combo's to advance. 3. finally focus on how each enemy fights. This game is a departure from the normal here is the first level, now we will walk you through the tutorial before letting you go HAM. Be patient and you will eventually make it through.

I really wanted to like and recommend this game. The art looks excellent, animations look fluid, the sound is ok too, I myself had been keeping an eye on this game for a while which makes writing this review kind of sad.
Where the game drops the ball is the gameplay. There are so many problems even playing the game the way the devs recommended, with a controller and everything the game still feels unresponsive, the hit detection feels awkward, trying to do anything after getting hit ended up being more of a gamble than anything else, there isn't any post hit invicibility or a considerable push back to give you space. Which means you won't always know for sure if you're getting hit until a monster brutally murders you in two or three hits. The dodge move was useless due to the start-up frames leaving you open to getting hit since it takes a bit to actually move away, attacking is actually quicker.
Speaking of attacking, even the input of the basic combo doesn't always respond as it should making it another gamble if you're trying to cancel the combo into a decapitation move to restore mana, sometimes I managed to pull it off perfectly but most times it felt like the game just refused to do it and it would either stop around the second hit or do the normal 3-hit combo despite me pressing the button only twice. Also getting the first hit due to how the controls respond also felt like I was making a bet rather than being skillful.
It all feels very loose, devoid of necessary feedback to the player. It needs to have tighter, more responsive controls that would allow to pull off moves and possibly tactics well which even if they pulled off I'm sure it would retain the level of challenge they were going for. But as it stands, during release, the game is difficult for the wrong reasons and quite a shame too since I really can't give it enough praises over how good and different it looks.
If you want a challenging 2D Platformer you're better off playing Volgarr the Viking or classics like the 2D Castlevanias, at least there the controls respond perfectly and the whole game feels tighter and meatier. Hopefully the devs will take the feedback and either patch this while looking at where other games got it right or do a better job on their next game. Personally I would like to see them fix this game by overhauling the gameplay and if they do I'd consider playing it all the way.

The Good: Great visuals and amazing music. Combat is challenging but fun - it's kind of like Zelda crossed with Dark Souls, because you have to time your attacks carefully and dodge the enemy attacks. Exploration is rewarding - tons of collectible upgrades to find. The puzzles in the dungeons are mostly clever and interesting, and the dungeons themselves are always well-designed and look cool. The design of the world is really impressive too, with different areas and obstacles and creatures to encounter.
The Bad: The movement can be a bit frustrating at times, as the game uses a fixed camera so you sometimes will jump expecting to land in one position and you'll end up falling or landing somewhere else. The story is difficult to follow at times because there's no dialogue - everything is conveyed by the characters pointing and gesturing - and sometimes I had no idea WHY I was going somewhere, I was just following the marker on the map. The map also doesn't show dungeon entrances, and since dungeons contain collectibles it's very difficult to find them later and collect 100% of the items.
Overall this is a very good game and I would highly recommend it for anyone who likes ARPGs with a focus on the Action, like Zelda, Dark Souls, or Torchlight.

I love this game. It runs flawlessly for me (GTX 980), which I'd expect given its age. Not sure how well it works on other hardware, so make sure to check other people's performance if you're concerned about your own setup being able to handle it.
It's a lot of fun, and looks as good as it's ever going to thanks to the polish it's received. Storyline might be confusing for some, but I'll try explain this as easily as I can while remaining conscious on this much Morphine: Nephilim are cross-dressers who like to get jiggy with dead bodies... Wait, no, wrong creeps, I was thinking of Aunt Robert - they were combinations of Angels and Demons. Because why not, right?  There were lots of them. They killed everything that moved.
The powers-that-be didn't like this and struck a deal with 4 such Neph: We'll give you supreme power if you f*** up anyone whose race starts with 'N' and ends with 'ephilim'. A few hours later, Death (who was known as Horace the Horrific at that point because of his Horrific taste in Halloween masks) cottoned on to what they meant, and he and his two Brothers, as well as his sister (called Fury, because... well, you know, 3000 years of PMS will do that to you, not to mention having 3 brothers who always leave the toilet seat up) decided to slaughter them all.
Stuff happened, more stuff happened after that, and then someone went and broke some Seals (the other Seals were so upset by this they all went Clubbing after the funeral)  which indicated the Apocalypse was meant to begin.
Except it wasn't, but that didn't stop War (known in some circles as 'Stoney Tony') from f***ing up big time and starting the Apocalypse accidentally himself. Oops. I told him to lay off the Pixie Dust, but would he listen? Would he f***.
With Humanity wiped out, Horace was all, "Goddammit Tony I can't take you anywhere AND PUT THAT BLUNT OUT FOR KANYE'S SAKE", so he then goes to try and reverse this catastrophic set of events, and prove Stoney's innocence.
Well, that and so he could get all stabby-slicey with the local demon populace.
Anyway, long story short, this game rocks, it looks good, it plays well now that it's fixed (devs fixed a catastrophic crash bug in 24 hours - hear that Rocksteady?) and the only complaints I know of right now are the fact that it doesn't run perfectly for everyone. Yeah, I know, it lags on Pocket Calculators, who woulda thought? If you don't already own it, then I've got some bad news for you - Horace will be COMING FOR YOU. Or was it ON you? Actually, yeah, that would be much worse.

I dont have as many hours as the original day-1 players.
I purchased the game during it's first sale for about thirty-five bucks.
Back then, the game was...decent...even after some much needed patchwork according to players/reviewers.
My adventures started off with a bang and then fizzled.
Basically, it was a game of just mining...and everything was the same no matter what planet I was on.
Gameplay got stale quick.
Since the last patch (1.32), the game has really taken off.
The addition of portals and a deeper "campaign" has made the gameplay more interesting.
And now, even the mining isn't so bad anymore.
The planets now look fantasic because of the new textures and added variation to flora and elements.
More ship variety and new alien races are a plus too.
Sadly, the animals still suck. They all still look and act pretty much the same. It's a total failure.
But please, don't let that dissuade you from getting the game.
The changes made have opened up a whole new world of adventure.
I have been going in cirlces becuase I just...FIND...stuff to get into.
It feels like being a pilot on my own trying to survive long enough just to get to where I'm going without being sidetracked...but I do.
So far, I'll give NMS a 7/10.
Pre-patch 1.32, it was a 4/10.
Currently, it's like minecraft on a diet.
A good game to add to your library.
However, I still say only get it on sale. (35 or below)
\----------------------------

I landed on this planet.

LOL

As soon as I left that rock's atmosphere, I landed in the lap of a dog fight with a pirate.

Made it to the floating space trading post on fumes and duck tape.
Long story short...left with new parts, money in my pocket, and another unsuspecting quest in tow.
The game is holding my attention pretty well now.
Hope they let us see each other soon!

Normally I do not write reviews. Often times I will read through the reviews before I buy the game. This is for those of you like myself! This game is undoubtedly challenging, if you want to go on a rampage and rush right at the enemy and expect to come out the other side alive, this may not be for you. However! The sheer chaos and mayhame of trying to stay alive and hold on to you position as a half dozen guys are trying to flank and kill you is somewhere between rage inducing and abstractly tactical.
Once you get the hang of the game you will soon find yout self promoted through the ranks, each rank unlocks additional gear and weapons. Soon a small fire team will be following you around, this allows you to focus on more tactical decisions. Where should I put up this sandbag? How am I going to tkae that hill with the MG on top? This is a sandbox warfare game, do you want to fight where the fighting is heaviest? Would you rather sneak around behind enemy line and sabotage communications and fuel depots?
In conclusion, this game is stunningly simple, breathtakingly audacious and yet deviously difficult to master and when you feel you have a hang of it stop by the multiplayer servers, there is a nice community for this game.

When I first started playing Running With Rifles, I hated it. I kept dying, over and over and over again. I couldn't get past Private, and I had no idea why.
I revisited it sometime later, and released my mistake. I had been attempting to lone-wolf it, much like something from Battlefield.
That's what makes the game interesting. If you're not with a good amount of people, you *will* die within seconds. Rather it be a stray grenade, or the enemy swarming you, you're doom is all but ensured if you go out on your own.
On a note about the enemy and allies, the AI is interesting. Sometimes it's amazing, and can complete an entire map on their own, without you doing anything. Other times, they refuse to do anything, and will walk around, or be near blind. The AI isn't bad, but it can be annoying at times.
Another thing I don't like, is how the objectives are placed along the map. They're often times placed in very odd, and useless locations. It would be fine, if the AI didn't use the objective locations to prioritize their attacks. Sure, they'll go to other places, but the main fighting force will go to the objective.
Overall, the map is good enough for a buy. Playing for extended periods can get boring, mainly due to the lack of progression you'll come across in certain bases. You can easily be fighting over the same area, getting control and losing control of it, for ten to twenty minutes, or even more.

Really funny and enjoyable shooter with amazing graphics. You can choose to play stealthily or run and gun. It has amazing animations and amazing characters.
You play as William Blazkowicz and you shootup Nazis. You start with a few cutscenes and then you will be able to pick which teammate you want to save, keep in mind this changes what happens in the game. This decision adds or removes some missions that you are able to do (doesnt effect achievement missions). Most importantly, it determines which signature weapon you receive. Save Wyatt for the Dieselkraftwerk and Fergus for the Laserkraftwerk.
Perks that are earned by killing enemies a certain way. There are items that you can pick up to upgrade your weapon. Your main hub is in a captured giant captured Nazi U-boat (submarine) and it changes as you continue through the story. More and more allies join you. You can explore the submarine and have you can even play the old wolfenstein game in the arcade area of the ship. It also has a shooting ranges and side missions/activieis and easter eggs for you to find/explore.
The main story is very short, but there are many other side missions you are able to do. In the beginning, the story is great and seems like a normal, but when you progress farther through the story, everything becomes really crazy. I found myself saying "what the ♥♥♥♥ did I just watch". The best way to describe it is: short, but really satisfying.
There a few difficulties to choose from and "I am death incarnate" difficulty is quite challenging. When you complete the story, you will be able to choose another difficulty setting called "mein leben" which gives you no saves. You must play it through from beginning to the end in one sitting. Completing the game on this setting also give you an achievement.
You can choose to dual wield weapons (doesnt have to be the same weapon) to give up a little accuracy for damage. You can run in guns blazing, or you can choose to play stealthily which adds a significant amount of time into one mission/level. You get the chance to choose one of three "abilities" in the main mission (but dont worry you can collect them all).
Lets you access smaller spaces.
Allows you to smash through walls, doors, and boxes.  You can kill Nazis with this ability as well.
Lets you reach higher platforms with extendable legs. You can also access different cover spots.
I personally recommend the Constrictor, it lets you squeeze into little holes that connect the rooms, and it lets you hide under containers, which you can then sneak attack Nazi's from.
The cutscenes are REALLY well done. The animations and movement of the characters are realistic. The level design is pretty good, similar to older shooters, but I find that it's pretty linear and sometimes they don't give you many options as to what you are able to do. It is a mix between open/linear levels. Many games have problems with directing players as to where to head next, but in this game, when you get stuck, there is a key (G by default) which indicates where your objective is located.
The main story can be completed pretty fast, but there are many other side missions, some of which give you upgrades to the abilities that you have. Even though the story is short, expect to take a while if you are looking to get all achievements or trying to get 100% (there are stats in game).
The game is really well optimized and has similar graphics to Doom. The particle effects are probably one of the most amazing parts of this game. The particle effects are beautiful, realistic, and really addicting to just watch.  When I first started up the game, everything was on the highest settings, this caused a lot of issues since the game has A TON of settings. I fixed this by turning down a few of the settings. Make sure to scroll down, the menu is minimalistic and it is easy to miss the "hidden" settings. I tinkered around settings for a bit and after turning down 3 or 4 things, it magically fixes everything. Pretty sure the people who are complaining about the optimization have potatos.....
I run the game perfectly fine at High/Ultra settings at 1440p with around or over 144 fps.
The music matches the game really well and you can tell they took their time in making it perfect. The music slowly changes as you start to get into action and changes when a commander alerts his soldiers or something significant occurs. It slowly layers on multiple sounds/instruments and it transitions into whatever action you take. The music in the cutscenes make you excited, much like watching a trailer for movie. It is comparable to the music in Doom because it has the guitars and drums and it really gets ur heart pumping as you jump and run around in game.
The default controls are pretty easy to get used to. It's similar to other shooters and you can rebind keys to suit whatever you need. It feels smooth, very very similar to Doom (cuz made by same people). Changing weapons is REALLY slow compared to Doom and I wish they could have made it faster for those people who are looking to run and gun.
So far, I've played Episode Zero. In this DLC, you get a taste of all of the DLC's to come. You play a little bit of each character, each with their own abilities. For example, when playing as Agent Silent Death, you makes less noise and enemies freeze when they spot you. Basically, it gets you hyped up for the DLC.
Easily worth the full price, even though it only has singleplayer. You can choose a different timeline which will change some of what happens in the game. The different abilities add more variation into the game, but its a pretty short campaign.

TNC ditched all of that and has gone for extraordinarily dull and meaningless locales. Even at one point late in the game where they do take you somewhere exotic, the area was still somehow an eyesore and absolutely no fun to traverse and shoot Nazis in.
The game also can't shake the feeling of being very rushed, right down to the main menu screen. Not to mention the exorbitantly small amount of actual playtime there is barring the long, long cutscenes and the game breaking bugs and crashes.

First up, I absolutely adore the original version of Darksiders 2, I can look past many of it's foibles and problems and would heartily recommend it to anyone with even a passing interest in this genre.
The main issues regarding the negative reviews ire twofold, firstly there was a crash that happens just after you select your save (or start a new one), click through the 'autosave' announcement, check your settings, then load, at this point the game crashed.  There is now a patch that has addressed this problem.
Secondly many negative reviewers are citing the pricing model as the main reason for the negative reviews.  While I can understand this can be infuriiating for some, that has NOTHING to do with the game itself.
On to the review...
The art style is fantastic, cartoony with just enough grit to make it feel different.
The texture work at the moment is spotty, with some fantastic and pretty high resolution/definition (for the game engine) model texturing but many of the world textures are still original, also including many of the weapons and armour you pick up during the course of the game.
The sound is flawlwss, as in the original, with all the grunts, slashes, and thumps you'd expect.  The voice acting is pretty good too, with certain voice actors hamming it up a little here and there.  The soundrtack is awesome, as before.
Unfortunately as of this moment, performance is woefull in placesl, a LOT worse than the original both at 30fps and 60fps there was a LOT of frame juddering, stops and starts, frame skips etc, the original ran a LOT smoother on my rig, although that may be down to the extra workload from the tweaked game engine.
After re-reviewing this game now I can actually play it I would reccomend it to those who can get it cheaply, and those who don't own the original.

So overall this game was enjoyable and I am going to play the sequel but I found it a little disappointing.
