The first thing I noticed was that the combat system is very similar to modern Batman games or Shadow Of Mordor. However, it seems more simplified, and timing attacks is not as important. What sets it apart from the other "Batman" games is that combos can be customized with different combinations of punches and kicks. I think there should have been more variety in the combo options, since they only come in 4 types: extra damage, reduce cooldown, health regen, and moves that multiply the effect of the previous move. Just when I think the game is about to get a little challenging, it throws me a bone and makes it too easy again. The player will sometimes be granted special abilities that can do anything from stunning all enemies, to controlling one robotic enemy at a time.
This game always boxes the player into an arena before starting a fight. Each boss fight ends with a quick-time-event where the correct sequence of buttons to press is always the same. I played on medium mode, and the combat was so easy for me, that I almost always ended each arena segment with full health. Sometimes, I'd take fall damage just before an arena, and end the arena with more health than I started it with.
Another similar feature to Batman games is the way climbing works in this game. It lends itself well to big, open, vertical world maps. Unfortunately, this game is extremely linear, and it's always very obvious which ledge to jump to next. There are a few secret items scattered around, but they're always just around a corner, and never extremely out-of-the-way. The game even notifies the player that there's a hidden item nearby by showing a picture of what the area around it looks like. There are a few obstacles, but they're pretty easy to avoid. Just check my achievements, there's one for being spotted by a drone 5 times, and I still don't have it after completing the entire game.
Most of the developer's focus was clearly put into the writing, setting, character design, and music. The premise of the story seems heavily inspired by Total Recall and other sci-fi films that focus on memory. The aesthetics look like they're somewhat inspired by Ghost In The Shell with some homages to it scattered around. My own hardware has some problems, and games tend to have graphical artifacts for me. It was difficult to tell in this game what was intentional artifacts and what was my bad GPU. The plot is very contrived and full of cliches, but I won't spoil it here. The idle boss chatter during fights can be a little dumb and repetitive.
Where this game really shines is the sound design and soundtrack. Again, my hardware is bad, so it was difficult to tell when the audio was glitching on purpose and when my hardware was acting up again. It has lots of glitchy aspects to it, like repeating and looping errors. The music definitely saved the game for me. The music made me want to get to the next easy arena fight just to listen.
I got this game from the Capcom Humble Bundle, and if you can get this game for practically free like I did, it's definitely worth playing for the "experience". Otherwise, there's no challenge or replay value, so I can't recommend paying the full price.

I just finished this game.  Steam has me clocked in at 11 hours.  11 hours of pure awesome if you ask me.  I went in not knowing what to expect.  And loved every minute of it.
First off I'll talk about the combat since thats one of the things people have a hard time enjoying about the game.  At first glance it looks like an Arkham game with the freeflow.  This is a mistake.  Its nothing like it at all.  Take everything Batman taught you about fighting and forget all about it.  This is far too different to even have that comparison.  Once you remove that the combat becomes more enjoyable.  Not to say its great.  The combat was the weakest part of the game but it was still fun IMO.
There is climbing that is pretty much completely ripped from Uncharted.  Which is fine.  Why fix what ain't broke?
Memory remixing.  The most unique gameplay element about this game is sadly lacking.  In a short game like this I can understand having only a handful but they give you just enough to make you want more.  Its lacking in depth.  Just find the glitches in the memory and activate them and find the right ones to change the memory.  And the game wastes no time telling you exactly what the memory should be changed to kinda removing the mystery.
Finally the story.  This is where the game truly shines.  Its one of the most compelling stories in a game I've experienced in a while.  The premise is kinda scary.  Memories can be tampered with even stolen and the results are not good.  Hey a video game protaganist with amnesia and there's a very good reason for it for once lol.  With a few good plot twists it was a real treat going through this story.
What makes me love the game so much is the little details.  Early in the game there are camera shots establishing a nice view of the city.  Finding the little bits of info on the world and history was also a treat.  And Nillin is another great female character.
Dontnod built a really cool world here and even if a sequel is very unlikely I am happy to have visited it.

I wanted to love this game so much. I played Life Is Strange, another DONTNOD title before this one, and was hoping for something similairly story driven. Will this big open area with a pit below it have invisible walls to give you some freedom, or have none so you need accuracy? Who knows! Over and over again, the game design was frustrating to the point of needing to take breaks to avoid throwing things. You know, I used to think highly of Activision because of the Call of Duty series. When this game came out, everyone was losing their♥♥♥♥♥♥and I include myself on that. Even back then this company was sh#tting bad multiplatform crap games that most people never liked, but this one made us all forget about it. Is it good, is it worth it? Well, with the next CoD of Duty having a remake of this game, I might as well bother to review this. And as usual, I'm going to start with the stuff it does poorly. Now there's not much to that, but the issues it has are big.
First and foremost, the autosave feature. Jesus #nal f#cking christ, remember when you could just save or quicksave in games!? This is one of the games that pushed the auto-save feature like it was the hot sh#t forward, like it or not. And I don't like it one bit, it's complete bullsh#t. Let me explain: Whenever the hell the game feels like, it will save. You have NO control over it, and the saves are at complete random. It can save twice in a row with barely a few seconds in between, or it might not even safe more than twice on a level. It's way more painful than you think, you can be fighting for over 5 minutes, suddenly get killed by a random RPG and suddenly have to replay most if not all of that. Even worse, it manages to ruin some of the best moments of the game. One of the missions that most people love of this game ends up with you, having to wait for an helicopter that's around 9 kilometers away. I got one auto save when that last objective was told, then I got another auto save when the helicopter was still 7 kilometers away. And guess what, those 7 last kilometers are around 6 to 10 minutes of intense shooting action with way too many enemies storming your place at the same time from all directions. And since I was playing on a high difficulty (more on that later), I died a lot, and had to replay the same area over and over. Bottom line, either have good auto-saves or just LET THE PLAYER SAVE MANUALLY.
The other issue this game has is, as I said, the difficulty. Is the game really difficult? No, mainly the different difficulty modes are a standard case of artificial difficulty. You know what changes? You can take more shots, which is normal, but it also changes the amount of grenades the enemies throw, and makes enemies see you as the main target, ignoring all other NPC's. DO YOU KNOW WHAT HELL LOOKS LIKE!? HOW ABOUT A SMALL CORRIDOR CONSTANTLY BEING STORMED BY GRENADES!? It gets REALLY OLD, REALLY FAST.
That being said though, this is easily the best CoD game there is. There's a reason why it's getting somewhat remastered on the new♥♥♥♥♥♥CoD. It really is a good experience.
The story, while most people would over-look it, it's quite entertaining and decent for all the♥♥♥♥♥♥CoD games get these days. It's not too complex but it's catchy enough for you to want to know what's next. It also isn't too long, which is a shame, but also includes a kickass extra level that aparently is supposed to be really hard, but I kind of beated it on my second try on the Hard difficulty.
Gameplay is also okay. You know how all CoD games after MW2 tried to constantly force the multiplayer unlockables into the story mode, as of to tell you "GO PLAY THE MULTIPLAYER INSTEAD YOU F#CKING♥♥♥♥♥♥"? That makes the gameplay feel stupidly shallow and that doesn't happen here. You get in one mission help from a helicopter, and later the ability to call for bombs thrown by jets, that's it. I wish more CoDs just did that. It also changes the pace multiple times instead of throwing countless enemies over and over, although it does have constant respawning npc's, something I don't like at all.
The mission "All Ghillied Up" deserves a mention of it's own. If you have played it, then you know why. It's one of the best levels I've ever played and sure as hell is memorable. It's quite inspired from games such as STALKER (funny enough I have no idea what the enemies talk about in this level but I did hear one♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ NPC mention a "Stalker" through the first stage of the level), and the soundtrack of it is just perfect. The second stage also ends strong, although as I said, it's painful on high difficulties because of the auto-save.
The graphics are also okay, which seems to be what most people are looking forward on the remastered edition, something that quite pisses me off. IT STILL LOOKS GOOD TODAY, YOU F#CKING IDIOTS! WHY WASTE THE MONEY BUYING A SH#T GAME FOR THE REMASTERED WHEN YOU CAN JUST BUY THIS!? The only bad thing the graphics have are the ocasional weird bugs, like NPC's ignoring each other even though they're supposed to be hostile and corpses freezing in mid air until you die and the game reloads an auto-save.
Lastly, the multiplayer. I must say I usually ignore the multiplayer aspect on these reviews, specially if the game is this old, however this game did it right. All these new CoD's just flood the game with upgrades and killstreak unlockables which completely miss the point of the modes to begin with, this one kept it really simple and it's fun. However good luck finding anyone to play with. I know for a fact that it still has a strong community, but once the remastered version comes out, I don't think anyone but old school fans will stick around.
Is this game worth it? Yeah. Is it worth the 20€ price-tag, though? Nah, it's good but not that much. I'd say, get it if it drops around 5€ or so, but get it if you're truly interested on it and might want to give the multiplayer a try. Otherwise, while it has really cool moments, you might wanna play something else instead.
TL;DR Edition: The good CoD game. Really good controls and story, although it has some cheap difficulty crap and a quite terrible auto-save feature. It also has a quite high price tag for how old the game is, if you're truly interested you better wait for a sale, but it's a really good game.

There is not much to say about this game that hasn't already been gushed about by other reviewers. The gameplay is smooth, well-done, and addictively fun. The classic themes and art style add a fresh and unique flavor to the characters that is unique to Skull Girls as a fighting game, while also fitting well with the 2D gameplay. All of the characters play in a unique manner, and are excellently balanced (which is CRUCIAL in a fighting game). Every DLC character is a delight to play and worth the money. There are a few things that make this game stand out to me though:
1. The Color Pallettes: Most fighting games just slap a bunch of colors together with no theme or purpose, and expect you to be dumb enough to purchase it anyway and pick one. Not Skullgirls. Skullgirls' Color Palettes (even the ones that come with the game, instead of the DLC) seem deliberate and have deliberate themes. The color-swaps look intentional and make each color change look like it had a reason for existing. For example, I love the yellow and black color theme for Big Band, as they have gone to great detail to make him look like either a mafia member or a 1900s sleuth from a classic detective movie. This is a detail was clearly handled with care; and for once, I feel like the color-palette DLC is actually worth buying, as there is a MASSIVE number of alternate colors to choose from.
2. The Story: The game developers went to insane effort to make a story that is actually compelling. This is a part of the game that a lot of other fighting game developers just loosely string together. However, the developers of Skullgirls designed each character to be unique and to feel like real people. It is done in a classic, visual feel that colorfully displays their passions, backstories, and what drives them as people. The characters feel very much alive.
3. The Characters Themselves: I've already made the point that the characters are great; but I wanted to hammer in the level of thought put into them with an example: Double is an evil, eldritch goddess that serves as your typical "uses-everyone-elses'-powers-to-mimic" character. However, she reminds me strongly of another character from a favorite fighting game of mine: Necrid from the incredibly successful "Soul Caliber II." The reason for this is that, like Necrid, her attacks were not sloppily slapped together. Balance and thought was put into each attack. This means that, while she mainly uses attacks from other characters, each attack was chosen in such a way as to ensure that she chain together seemlessly and without making her weak or overly cheap. Each attack feels natural, and their odd, but good combinations make her feel like a unique character in her own way, just like Necrid.
4. The DLC: Normally, I would dislike this much DLC in a game. For players who don't have a lot of money to spend, this game's DLC is hard to buy, as there is a lot of it. You'll probably want to grab it on sale. However, I feel that the developers did the DLC system justice by not abusing it. Most of the DLC was made after the games release, which means that instead of making us pay for extra stuff that should have just been in the game, the developers gradually keep adding more and more to the game, which is what DLC IS MEANT TO BE ABOUT! I have a lot of respect for developers who keep adding to the game after release, expanding the lore; and I feel that it's entirely reasonable that they be paid for the effort. That being said, each DLC adds a lot of value to the game and is totally worth the money. You will not be disappointed with your purchases, as they do NOT cut corners with anything.
5. Controller Compatibility: I had no trouble configuring a wide variety of USB controllers to this game, which makes it a lot easier to play local matches with friends on the couch.
In conclusion, this game has become my favorite fighting game on Steam, for good reason. It is fun, querky, and a delight to play. (I also thought the Credits Song was deep, in a creepy way, as it is about the Skull Heart.)
Compare to: the "Guilty Gear" series, the "Blaz Blue" Series, and Street Fighter.

TL;DR - Woulda, coulda, shoulda been amazing, but it's just not that good. Any art in it was destroyed by PC morons on the production crew who rely on gimmicks to make the game longer than it would be naturally. It's like expecting Bach and getting Slipknot.
Ok, I wanted to like this game, I really did.
First - I consider New Order to be one of the greatest games I've ever played in terms of the world it built and the feels it made. Seeing your friends sacrifice themselves, love, loss, tough choices, and a sense of versimilitude that few games really equal. It was AMAZING.
New Colossus had little of that. Kept the engine - good. Kept the characters, good. Make a new base and a good plot reason to move the fight to the US... good.
Thats where the good stopped. The rest of the game is RELENTLESS politically correct crap, slanted so heavily as to destroy any sense of versimilitude or art in the game. Here are my problems and why:
-The KKK being in charge in the south. (Yes, they were actually a political force in America's past, I'm fine with them being in the game - they actually existed. More than that, up until the mid 1940s, they had many sucessful, middle class members. My problem is twofold: First, it stretches credulity, but not far, to portray a leadership corps for administrating the US as coming from this pool - its not realistic. Second, they are portrayed as two-dimensionally 'all white people is evil'. The actual civil rights movement had a huge number of white allies. That is absent from the game.)
- Harlem blacks being point on the U.S. resistance. (My problem is that this choice sacrifices realism for the sake of being PC. I mean, really? All the white people just rolled over and took it? It doesn't stretch credulity to think a subsociety such as Harlem blacks would stick together in the face of an occupation, but when this plot device is set against the local enemy of the KKK, the game can't even pretend not to be trying to make some kind of racial statement. Furthermore, it made sense to have Caroline be the leader in the first game. She was a hardened, trained professional and officer and Blaskowitz had worked with her previously. One Caroline dies, black chick becomes leader without so much as a memo being issued. The team had a REASON to trust Caroline - she won that trust. Once she dies, why is the other one in charge?)
- A few scenes that are frankly macabre seemed to be added in for no reason other than to shock. Portraying Hitler as a decrepit, senile, incontinent, volatile old man WAS funny, and if you wanted to love to hate someone, that seems ok. However, the scene where, Anya, a woman who is about 8 months pregnant with twins yet still on active combat duty makes an acrobatic leap to tackle you, sheds her top to the skin (which was on fire - I guess as an excuse to take it off) and kills a Panzerhund with a machine gun under each arm, boobies flapping, screaming, and covered in blood is simply bizarre. In most movies that nonsensical stunt would have earned a Rotten rating on Rotten Tomatoes.
That said, the game isn't ALL bad. The addition of combat Gadgets (the stilts, bull-rush and constrictor harness) open up many new options in HOW you play the game, even if it really just mostly takes you 50 ft out of the way to enter a room from a new angle. The bits with Hitler WERE funny, and Super Spesh was one of the best characters I've seen in a game. The bit with the head-in-a-jar was ridiculously over the top, but if we're talking about super-science invented by ancient Jewish scientists in a secret order, I guess that's just par for the course. Also, the bits with seeing BJ's childhood were cool, even if the racist aspect was far too over the top. *I* certainly never conceived of Blaskowitz as being an emotionally traumatized runaway raised by a racist daddy before this game. I don't think it really mattered to his character before this game decided it needed to matter.
Still, those new bits don't compensate for a number of bizarre choices in directing, a plot that is MUCH less tight than New Order, the fact that this game sacrifices realism and art in favor of the PC aspect, and that the game relies on making you play minigames to artificially extend the play time. Wait till this game drops to sub $20. It's just not that good.

Fantastic game, but also dissapointing in a way.
Wolfenstein's modern reboot returns with a highly anticipated sequel, which seems to learn from DOOM, and past games, but at the same time forgets things that made the first great. The game presents a fantastic story, which is a lot bolder and excited to tackle more themes that the original didn't. This one has an insanely original story, with some intense moments, and an amazing cast. In this sense, it is better than the original. The gameplay seemed to be a bit more fast paced, and it encouraged much more movement than the first game, which makes for some awesome fights, though not as great as DOOM, but better than mostly every other generic shooter. The level design is what truly dissapoints in this one, since the first game had amazing levels with so many branches and ways to tackle the objective, while this one presents a few basic options, and feels a lot more linear.  The campaign also seemed quite short, though there are multiple side objectives you can do if you feel like expanding your play time. The difficulty seems higher than the original, which is great for those seeking for a challenge, but for those seeking a good time with a great story, less difficult modes exist. Every difficulty seems very well made, but higher dificulties can be very frustrating. Most issues seemed to be fixed, though crashing might still be frequent (in my playthrough, crashes were rare, but happend 2 or 3 times).
Bassically, it beats the original in some aspects, but the level desing and some other things are much more limited in this one. Great game none the less.

Игра, не требовательная к ресурсам, пойдет и на слабых машинках. Используется регдолл-физика, в геймплее есть прокачка персонажа, покупки, достижения. Помимо основной сюжетной линии, есть дополнительные уровни: Арена (сражения с толпами врагов), Грим (подземелья с тварями), Хаммербол (забей мяч молотком в ворота противника). Может есть и другие, пока недоступные для меня.
Можно прокачивать одновременно несколько персонажей, со своим инвентарем и достижениями.
Список оружия впечатляет, есть мечи, моргенштерны, молотки, топоры, стреляющее оружие. Одновременно в руке (?) можно иметь два вида оружия, причем в игре они могут сцепляться вместе. Доступное оружие находится в Холле, где можно докупать всё необходимое. В оружие можно вставлять камни (которые даются по ходу игры или добываются в Гриме), тогда у оружия появляются дополнительные свойства. Можно покупать броню и метательное оружие (кинжалы, звездочки), а также различные бомбы. Также есть "порции здоровья", что помогает на высоких уровнях.
В целом мне игра нравится за быстрый геймплей, можно отвлечься на нее на 15 минут, чтобы пройти очередной уровень. Также нравится физика игры, реально ощущаешь тяжесть или легкость оружия и брони. Дополнительную реалистичность придает то, что размахивать оружием приходится буквально самому, т.е. мышкой раскручивать меч, чтобы получить более сильный удар.

At the beginning there was nothing.
Well alright, maybe not nothing, but definitely not what most of the people expected - what was presented to the Hello Games perfectly by more than 80% negative reviews on Steam. I myself enjoyed the game from the start, as I loved the exploration, the hope, that the next planet will be a lush one. I enjoyed great views and the journey - even if it did not lead to something great or ground-breaking (story-wise).
But now, after a year and 3 massive updates, I feel that Hello Games made this game even better, especially for the people who were initially disappointed. First of all, we have 4 different game modes - normal, harder and hardcore mode (where you character dies permanently) for those who like the survival side of the game and are looking for a challenge. The 4th one is a creative mode, where you do not have to farm and grind and can just enjoy the universe, the exploration side of the game and build a base of your dreams.
Secondly, we got three types of ground vehicles to move faster on the surface and explore more. You can also build your own base with crafting stations, storage and decorative structures. You can buy big cargo ships, additionally to your own, which can store massive amount of items.
And finally, with the most recent update, we got (beta) multiplayer, which works great now, but hopefully will be developed to even a better version with the next update. We received portals by which you can travel fast across solar systems or end up in a random planet. We now can summon our ship, so no more boring returns when you ventured too far on the surface exploring. The graphics got a massive overhaul and now looks muuuuch better. And we got QUESTS, which are also generated procedurally. Plus, a story has been revamped, to fit all the introduced mechanics and should now give around 30h of gameplay.
In my eyes the game has been worth the price from the very beginning, but was not ready for the majority of players who were looking in it something different. Right now, after these three updates I feel confident that they will find what they were looking for. It is a completely different game that it has been a year ago!
More than 10 000 people playing this game right now cannot be wrong!

I've only played this game because it was made by Dontnod and had to try it after finishing Life is Strange. Ofc I didn't expect anything closer to that in quality but thought it worth a try. And well, yes it did. It's a good game. Not great but not bad either. It's just a good game.
I recommend it but only if you like TPS hack and slash games (DMC, God of War, Darksiders etc.) and platformers (like Tomb Raider for example). Because the game is the combination of these two genres. You either playing a platformer going through Neo-Paris and its buildings or fighting the enemy. There isn't too much "downtime" in the game.
The art and music are gorgeous but not everything is the outside... And here lies the problems. Mostly two big things.
1. The main "selling point" of the game, the memory remix, is limited. You will only use it _FOUR_ times in the whole game and only in scripted scenes. And it's a sequence puzzle nothing more. That's a big letdown, I was expecting something like Watch Dogs where you can interact with everyone...
2. The game is incredibly linear and the combat is even more repetitive. You basically do the same thing through the whole game from the first minutes until the very last. To make it worse the combat system is broken in the sense that you can chain your abilities together in a way that you will never die... Not that it's bad but makes the whole game really really really easy (final boss fight was like 3 mins long max).
The story is pretty good and that's why I kept playing. Once again it's not Life is Strange level but you can see and feel it was made by Dontnod. Can't tell anymore about it because otherwise I'd spoil it...
Give it a shot, but only buy it on sale (5€ max)

Cookie-cutter console formula with absolutely nothing new, but it does the basics well enough. Bare minimum for an "OK" game, but I would recommend several other games before this one. On sale for less than $10 its a fair purchase.
NOTE: My playtime is overly high because I idled in the menu.
PROS:
-Despite all the negatives/neutrals, I still had fun (but I'm not really sure why lol).
-Good length for what content there is. Game doesn't try to outlast itself. Just as I found it starting to get stale, it ended.
-EXCELLENT backstory/setting (but they did so little with it!)
-Despite the overall bad writing, some good lines.
-Scaramech collectibles are well hidden (all others are not due to level design, not due to the items themselves)
NEUTRALS:
-Combat is simple but efficient. The combat lacks depth though so it starts to get stale fast (see build your own combo cons)
-Level design is generic and linear with obvious side branches to pickup collectibles. (My first and only playthrough without trying to get collectibles I got 84% completion. This is too high in my opinion and the collectibles are too obviously placed)
CONS:
-Plot is terribly paced with zero progression during levels then major progression between levels (this is especially unfortunate as the backstory is pretty amazing).
-Plot is basically a bad Hollywood screenplay. Very predictable.
-Cutscenes are NOT SKIPPABLE. Really?
-Cutscenes are often slow with very little action and a character simply talking.
-"MEMORY REMIX" sequences are basically trial and error (which you have to watch through each time). INCREDIBLY TEDIUOS esp considering its trial and error.
-Build your own combo is misleading. "Build your own combo" thing doesn't change any of the combt moves, it simply makes the predefined punches/kicks do either dmg, cooldown reduction, or healing, but the actual order of punch/kick is the same.

Given the magic that's literally this game's theme, I already can't recommend it. Wasn't intending on going over the 2hr. limit, but lo and behold I've lost my $50 EC to the dregs of time. [Why there isn't a rent option on Steam, I don't know.]
Funnily enough, that's not the only issue that wants to make itself glaringly apparent. There is a lot of running back and forth in this game, as is expected, but it becomes glaringly annoying when you get to a point that's right in front of the thing you have to get to, looks like you can reasonably walk or jump to it, and then get your hopes, dreams, aspirations and patience (much of which has dwindled down from all the zigzagging nowhere) blocked off by and cast into the chaos that is invisible walls. Granted this would be rectified by the time you figure it out, giving you a sense of accomplishment. For me it's just continual annoyance at how much this game costs even at pre-order price.
So when you figure out one confusingly area-wide puzzle. you are then faced with the next question: where the hobscat do I go now? The map only helps to an extent, probably for good reason. But then there's those other times when you get to a thing at the south of the screen that looks attainable from where you're standing, but can't.
Which brings us to the elephant's flatulent infant: the camera. I know the whole point of the camera switching from top-down perspective to 3D is to get a gander at the scenery and even actually show you where the thing you're supposed to get to is, but:
- the theme of the game already ruined the first for me to begin with.
- after you go past this point, finish dealing with it and have to take the path back, you have to deal with it again. This isn't helped by the fact that even on the lowest settings, in open areas, even underwater at times, the game lags immensely. It also seems that the camera is actually an elephant when it does this as it struggles to actually keep up with you, and if you're running off to a cliff facing ground 3-4 blocks below you, tough luck.
Combat's alright, but not as fleshed out as it could've been. The decision to make the moveset expandable through schematics well-hidden in areas seems like a good move....then you realize that some of these moves are just common sense to have on the get-go, and by the time you get them, you might actually be on your way to finishing the game: unless you're stuck dealing with the amazing question of where to go and what needs to be done to get a move on. Not to mention one of your abilities gets no love after its acquisition. You don't even get to use it on enemies unless they have certain things to target with it. Really? The one other legit power you get aside from your charge fist and you don't even try to flesh that out, Runic? I know the enemy variety is scarce but sheesh.
All in all: don't buy this game. My own "bias" aside, you're more than likely to waste a bunch of minutes just trying to figure out where you have to go, then going to the same spot constantly before you get to how scarce the game feels on the ~action~ side of things. And when you do get to where the game "gets good," your disappointment will be worsened by the fact that you can't get a refund.

Disclosure-I haven't played the game all that long so this is based upon initial first impression. I also am friends with some of the devs but whilte I was given a Beta key it was after i'd already been gifted the game by a (non-developer) friend. Even so I've indicated that I did receive a copy from Runic. That said here's my initial review which I will update as soon as I finish the game. Feel free to ask me any questions in regards to the game and I'll do my best to answer them.
I love the way this game communicates ideas without using a known language. it's like watching a Jim Henson production. Like Dark Crystal where the Skesis had this strange language and communicated via noises yet you could immediately tell what they were 'saying' via body language. Kudo's to the animators who worked on this because that part is amazing.I do wish It zoomed a little closer in during those few short but sweet dialog moments. Then again I wish we could zoom in in general. I'd really love to take a closer look at all the creatures. The creature design in this game is so fantastic.
My biggest issue is getting lost and not having any idea where to go. There are things I can't access because I lack upgrades and the areas are so big I end up losing track of where I've been. Checking the map doesn't help as it's a bit confusing to read. I'm not usually this terrible at games like this which leads to my getting frustrated now and then. Fortunately the 'Ah!' moments and story more than make up for it. Visual-wise however this is a beautiful game. Runic has managed to create a style of artwork that stands out from the rest of the games I've played over the last few years. Most textures have an almost animated quality to them with rich mood-setting colors breathing life into its naturalistic world. It features a mix of natural and steampunk yet without it being cliche. It feels like the setting is its own time and place rather than trying to fit into a specific genre.
The character designs are all unique and help add to the feeling of this place being a real live world. My only nitpick about it is that the ground textures seem almost an afterthought and a bit too simplistic compared to the rest of the environment. It pulls you out of the world a bit so hopefully they'll give those an upgrade at some point.
The music is wonderful and deserves its own section. A little surprising given I'm used to Matt Uelmen's music being a bit more thematic but the looser, more mystical nature of the melodies fits perfectly. It sounds wonderful through headphones and really blands in with the environmental sounds. It melds into this cohesive living landscape of sound that makes the environment feel so much more alive. There are all these little rhythmic touches that hearken back to his older work yet never in a way that sounds too derivative. Instead it sounds like the result of a gradual maturation of skill. As much as I love his past scores I'd consider this his best work yet. So much more subtle that his previous work but that's what makes it all the more magical.
I can tell that this games maps are a definite progression from Torchlight and Torchlight II's. The way everything fits together seems almost haphazard at first but then when you start to piece things together it starts making you feel like you're just barely uncovering pieces of this huge living machine. It's rather breathtaking in scope at times. I guess that's why I'm getting so frustrated. I want to see more of this amazing world. It can be a head-scratcher and calls for a measure of patience but the thrill of seeing the entire world around you change is worth its more frustrating moments. It's great for those looking for a mix of exploration with a bit of combat but if you're looking for pure action it's probably not for you. You're going to spend more time looking for clues and solving puzzles than you are fighting and what fighting there is seems to be a bit shallow.
All in all It's a really great if at times a little frustrating puzzle/platformer full of Henson-like characters and moodiness reminiscent of films like The Dark Crystal or animated films like Don Bluth's Secret of Nimh.

At the beginning there was nothing.
Well alright, maybe not nothing, but definitely not what most of the people expected - what was presented to the Hello Games perfectly by more than 80% negative reviews on Steam. I myself enjoyed the game from the start, as I loved the exploration, the hope, that the next planet will be a lush one. I enjoyed great views and the journey - even if it did not lead to something great or ground-breaking (story-wise).
But now, after a year and 3 massive updates, I feel that Hello Games made this game even better, especially for the people who were initially disappointed. First of all, we have 4 different game modes - normal, harder and hardcore mode (where you character dies permanently) for those who like the survival side of the game and are looking for a challenge. The 4th one is a creative mode, where you do not have to farm and grind and can just enjoy the universe, the exploration side of the game and build a base of your dreams.
Secondly, we got three types of ground vehicles to move faster on the surface and explore more. You can also build your own base with crafting stations, storage and decorative structures. You can buy big cargo ships, additionally to your own, which can store massive amount of items.
And finally, with the most recent update, we got (beta) multiplayer, which works great now, but hopefully will be developed to even a better version with the next update. We received portals by which you can travel fast across solar systems or end up in a random planet. We now can summon our ship, so no more boring returns when you ventured too far on the surface exploring. The graphics got a massive overhaul and now looks muuuuch better. And we got QUESTS, which are also generated procedurally. Plus, a story has been revamped, to fit all the introduced mechanics and should now give around 30h of gameplay.
In my eyes the game has been worth the price from the very beginning, but was not ready for the majority of players who were looking in it something different. Right now, after these three updates I feel confident that they will find what they were looking for. It is a completely different game that it has been a year ago!
More than 10 000 people playing this game right now cannot be wrong!

Spooky's House of Jump Scares tells the story of a nameless protagonist who ends up transcending 1000 rooms in a creepy house to try and escape. There's no big backstory to how we ended up here, and the narrative as a whole is loose with only sprinkled information from notes left behind by people who were here before you, and hints of who Spooky actually is. As you descend further into the house, you get stalked by strange and varied monsters...
The game is a free game, and is completely worth playing, but I'm going to start this review being critical of the game's biggest single glaring flaw; repetition. The idea of getting through 1000 rooms is a goal that is fun on paper, but can be quite tedious in execution. A lot of the rooms have randomized layouts, but only a finite of these layouts exist, so you end up going through the same rooms over and over again, and most of these rooms are empty and are made just to rush through. Which, as a result, makes it so that you end up running through hundreds of rooms with nothing really going on, On occasion you end up finding a note, or in a room with something more interesting, but even these can suffer from repetition. There's an Arcade Machine room you can get, which has 2-3 games to play, but are brief and only expanded with another game once (and a secret towards the end), there's a database room describing the monsters, but it's only updated every few hundred rooms you overcome. There's a room involving going the right path through doors to solve a simple puzzle you'll probably have to do 10-20 times before the game is up. On occasion, you'll start being chased by a monster as you go through these random rooms, but many of the monsters have the same basic strategy to escape from them (with only a few being exceptions), so you end up just running through rooms anyway.
This repetition is a shame, since it is sprinkled with legitimately good content and moments, so much so I would say the game is worth playing just for them. While a lot of the game is randomized, the best part of Spooky's House of Jump Scares is the scripted moments. The game will lock you in a unique location you are free to explore that delves into more narrative, and provides more unique gameplay scenarios, ranging from hiding in closets from a stalker enemy to crawling through a colorful child's area at a fast food restaurant. Without a doubt, these moments are the best part of the game, they present a variety of interesting scenarios (many wearing some obvious inspiration of other horror games on its sleeves), and make for an interesting ride whenever they pop up.
The monsters are varied in design and function. There's something like 13 monsters in the game, and they come with some deliciously gruesome and creepy death scenes should you fall to them. Now, they do all behave differently. There's a monster that can crawl out of holes around the environment to pop-up closer to you, a monster that changes the wall textures to a bloody red to make finding your way out harder, a monster you have to look at or else it'll attack you... But with the exception of a few like the last one, most of them unfortunately are tackled the same way... You just run like hell and dash through doors as fast as you can. The added applications are interesting, but in most cases, do very little to switch-up how you approach tackling them; ie, running away.
Still, I found the game to be enjoyable, a delight sometimes, and I may overstate its repetition. The game is free, and takes about 3-4 hours to complete. There's two different endings, and a number of fun scenarios sprinkled throughout the sort of dull middle randomized room segments. And, yes, the game may make you jump and scare you sometimes. Spooky's House of Jump Scares is a solid free horror game that has some definite highs, but maybe 1000 rooms was a bit much.

This is one hell of a game, though not without its misgivings.
CONS:
- The battle system could have been better. It's not awful, but don't expect Devil May Cry. This does not mean there isn't any variety to it, so you won't exactly get bored of it.
PROS:
- An interesting story with a fleshed out setting. A real rollercoaster. There's lots of external material you should look up later on, too.
- The art direction and the environments, goddamn! One alley in this game is more detailed than entire maps in other games. Maybe I'm overstating things, but only just a little - it's just insane how much detail is packed into everything.
- The music is also something else. They added a bit of a glitchy spin to it, so it definitely stands out and stands strong.
OVERALL:
Absolutely worth at least one playthrough to experience the story, and all the sights and sounds on offer. Despite the fact the combat system may have been a late addition, the game nevertheless is still a solid package in every other aspect. Its art direction, in particular, is just jaw-droppingly impressive and immersive.
Just... wow.

I'm going to say this right now: which control freak ruined this game?!
Because seriously, the entire game is about rigid CONTROL. From the way you crowd-control enemies to the completely linear path to your control freak partner Edge, you can practically hear the game screaming "Control is good, control is the source of all happiness" while it ignores all the destruction and chaos that excessive control causes!!!
Don't get me wrong, the game IS awesome. If you needed movie scenes you could pluck them from the visuals, and the camera intentionally stops to look at these architectural marvels. Accompanying this is an intriguing setting about humanity slowly reaching the singularity and creating monsters, both murderous and outright useful, to the point that they're tearing out pieces of themselves trying to reach it. Combat is also exquisitely dynamic, as you can change your tactics and outright change your buffs on the fly by altering the sequence of your button mashing while you focus on dodging relentless enemy attacks in the battlefield, only stopping when your fists can't punch something and you need to figure out the right gadget or power to solve the problem, and then going straight back into the fight.
But the game ultimately deals with the story by directly ordering your every non-combat action through Edge and the HUD, there's no alternate path you can take whatsoever, and the few options the game has (Combo Labs and Memory Remixes) are so tedious and methodical you'll be too sick of them to like what freedom you do have. Nevermind the fact that *spoiler* Edge performs a major terrorist act mid-game, or that Niln is a freedom fighter who ultimately mind-controls the bad guys and takes over */spoiler*; apparently, the fact that they're using control "for the greater good" means they're the good guys no matter how much chaos they cause! Sheesh, what an idiotic riot, the story ultimately hit a dud and was forced to use conventional cliche plot twists near the end because of the railroading. Ultimately, I wouldn't be surprised if some jackass in charge forced the game to be less and less of a sandbox until it became their movie about how unopposed control solves everything.
Seriously, why don't you make make a sequel, and make it open-world. ANYTHING to show the world that you and the people around you have choices, not blind obdience.

This game is a real mixed bag.
First, the negatives:
The story is completely bonkers and relies on made up words to create the sense of an otherworld, but as a result is just confusing as all hell.
The graphics, while nice, obscure the gameplay.  You can't easily tell foreground from background, and the smoke and light effects obscure combat.  In a twitch game this is pretty close to unforgiveable.
The difficulty is incredibly uneven.  A number of fights start with the enemy barrelling toward you, which means forced restarts.
The armory / weapon selection is pretty pointless.
The controls are entirely mouse based, despite the fact stuff like throwing weapons or activating guns could  have been better handled via keyboard.
The Hammerball game is ♥♥♥♥ing garbage, and if you select the mission you have to play it several times.
The game is just real janky.
But then the positives:
When it works, the combat is really really fun.  The control scheme is simple (just move your mouse around) but when you're fighting a series of challenging enemies it's just so much fun to tear through them, dodging attacks as you prep your own.  There is planning involved because of the need to attack via rotation.
There appears to be meaninful choice in story progression.  I haven't run through more than once, but there are divergent mission selection points as well as pure story options.
The graphics are nice and evoke an otherwordly Dune type theme.
The missions are short, so even with the uneven difficulty, they aren't too much of a slog.  And more than that, there is an ability to skip missions after you fail them several times, though I did not use it.
Overall, it's worth a playthrough if you have it, at least for an hour or so to see if you can stick out the jankiness to get to the heart of the game.  The main game itself is only like 4 or 5 hours long.

Assassin's Creed is the first game in one of Ubisoft's trademark franchise. A game which started off as a spiritual successor to the Prince of Persia series quickly grew into massive IP of its own. Although it's the first in the AC franchise Assassin's Creed is far from a great game. It has its pros that grew to define the franchise for what it is and also several cons that needs to be address. The game is set in the year 1191 during the height of the Third Crusade between the Muslims and Christians. The game covers several Middle Eastern locations which are rarely seen in gaming such as Jerusalem, Damascus and Acre. It's great to see Ubisoft tackle this sort of environment in a more historical setting than what modern Middle Eastern looks like. The environment feels immersive in its on way with Crusade guards along corner, horse riding in the frontier and also sword fighting. You play as Altair, an arrogant master assassin in the Assassin Brotherhood who has lost his title due to his own pride. Throughout the course of the game you're tasked with eliminating nine Templars while questioning the motives behind the assassination an your Brotherhood itself. The story is rather forgettable because it basically involves you moving from one city to another assassinating on Templar member to another which felt repititive. The only redeeming factor is probably the plot twist at the end.
The gameplay of Assassin's Creed is more of an action adventure game with added stealth mechanic. You can hide with scholars, on benches with citizens and also in hiding spots like stacks of hay. Movement in this game is rather annoying as Altair's running feels more like robot than an agile assassin with a poor camera control on top of it. Climbing also suffers from the same problem with some aspect of the building looks climbable but actually isn't. The combat of the game also doesn't par that well. Although it is still requires more skills than in future installments. You can't just swing your sword to easily kill all of the enemies as some enemies can actually counter and block. There's also no button prompts for counter so timing your counter is crucial. The stealth section of this game is kind of useless because sometimes guard can even detect you even if you're behind a wall. Even with all the research and eavesdropping about your current target, assassinating them stealthily is still a challenge bacause of the bad AI.
With all that being said, Assassin's Creed is still a worthwhile game especially for die hard fan of the series. Even though it has its flaws here and there it is still pretty enjoyable being able to run across rooftops and escape from guards and also fighting hordes of enemies at a time. For a of a franchise the game is okay as it leaves a lot of room of improvement and I would gladly give it a score of 6/10.

Honestly, I could've gotten other things with $12.75 (Arma 3 DLC is looking good) but even though I doubt it sometimes, I would still choose this game over anything just for the unique feel it gives.

This is one of the best games I've played this year so far, and it was only $20.
Imagine if Zelda and Journey has a baby and it was a metroidvania title. Thats Hob. Its combat is simplistic yet has depth to it. It can be button mashy (especially in the beginning) but as the game goes on the enemies become harder and the combat begins to evolve and get deeper.
The puzzles are challenging and fun to solve, similar to that of Zelda. You also get upgrades as you progress through the game to both your combat abilities and your "Glove" abilities which are mostly used for enviornmental puzzles, but can ALSO be used in combat. This is a pretty great system and I love it.
There are places and area (specifically in the beginning) where you might not have the ability or upgrade needed to get to or unlock a certain area. This is where the metroidvania style comes into play. These are almost all (atleast so far for me) optional upgrade items, like a heart piece, or a mana brick, but useful none the less for those of us willing to take the time to back track and find them.
The story telling is almost purely through the enviornment, and this is where the Journey feel comes from. There is no dialogue, which might sound like a negative, but I really dig it. I'm not sure exactly why I'm doing what the characters are doing, but I do know I'm having fun doing it, and I can see things in the enviornment that seem like subtle clues as to whats happening in this world. Speaking if which I LOVE the art design and direction. The Music is also top notch as well, really setting the mood and tone.
This game has barebones requirements to run on your PC and for only $20 I simply CANNOT recommend this game enough. I should note, I am only 2 and a half hours or so into the game but man I am really digging this game. Two thumbs up.

It's in the name: it's a house of jumpscares. It's cute cardboard cutouts of monsters that pop out once in a while to scare you. It's pretty much like jumping out and saying, ''Boo!'' in white bedsheets.
and it
still
worked
on
me
The jumpscares work because of the sudden musical/sound cue when they appear, their abrupt appearance on-screen, and the build up to them. You can go 20 rooms without anything happening, but the fact that something CAN happen is what leads to tension that is ultimately released when a blob pops up on-screen. The rooms play with your mind; incredibly narrow corridors where you KNOW something is coming (but doesn't), a large dark room where you see five candles in the distance, and even the use of grain filters in other rooms. The rooms get more macabre as the game continues and it really builds some eerie atmospheres.
Then there are the creatures that are just as cutely drawn as everything else, but still manage to spook you when they suddenly appear behind you. The music changes and you play run-away as you run through many rooms to escape, perhaps engaging with a jump scare or two on the way. Some of the later creatures have these characteristics that actually tense me the ♥♥♥♥ up when im running from them, like the girl saying 'come here'. Maybe I'm a ♥♥♥♥♥ but I got legit spooked and slightly fearful during some of the chases.
For it's simplicity it's an incredibly effective game. At just over 300 MB it manages to contain over 700 rooms, partially because it reuses rooms. But this manages to come into play in the atmosphere, as you wonder if you've already been in an area before, and the game uses that to further mess with your mind.
With each room being completed in less than three seconds, it becomes an addictive grinding affair as you race to the 50th floor of each area (save point and elevator located there). Each elevator taken leads to a change in scenery and the introduction of new characters. See, each 'area' has notes left by characters (never seen on-screen). They're actually pretty funny, like the character hoping he isn't a side-character leaving notes for, in his own words, ''pointless exposition''. Towards the end he realizes he's expendable because he didn't have an origin story at the beginning. Then there's the guy that went to the house for work.
It's Free to Play, it's a 300 MB download, it's premise is a game that actually scares you while being deceptively cute in its art, and it's addictive due to note-finding, new creatures introduced, and floor grinding for new scenery. Strongly recommended because this game is a lot better than it has ANY right being, given how little it has. Part of it has to be with how arcade-like it feels; real simple to play, real easy to get into, real easy to put down and no convoluted exposition. It's really simple, but that fact that it makes the most of its resources and is free (very important) gives it a recommendation. Its also legitimately spooky as it continues, which is odd given the artstyle.

Impire is a real time strategy game developed by Cyanide Studios. The game was released in early 2013 on PC.
Gameplay in Impire is heavily inspired by Dungeon Keeper. You are in control of a demon, and you have to build your own dungeon, with a large amount of rooms to build and modify however you want; along with building tunnels connecting all of the rooms together, you can create some really interesting dungeons.  The action in Impire is based around having squads of other demons, these squads consist of four demons, and they operate as a team, think of them as like a 4 man group out of an MMO, you want to have a tank, a healer and some damage dealers.  You are able to unlock new demons using the talent tree, which interestingly resets at the start of each level, allowing you to only spec into what you really are going to need for the objectives. Impire also has another game play element, called Raids. This function allows you to send your squads of minions on mini raids to other dungeons in order to gather treasure, materials, or complete side quests – this is nice addition but can sometimes be forgotten about if you aren’t careful.  The raids require no human interaction other than you telling the squad to go and start it.
The graphics in Impire will again, remind you completely of Dungeon Keeper, they just have a more higher resolution look to them. The UI in Impire can look daunting upon a first glance, but the game has a very good tutorial mission which explains everything very clearly and you’ll be navigating through the menus with ease after completing it. It would have been nice if all of the buttons came with a tooltip though, so you can just remind yourself as to what some of the lesser used buttons do at times without having to just click it to find out.
This game is fully voice acted to a pretty high standard,  the game is narrated very well, units are all voice acted. The game has quite an abundance of cut scenes with multiple characters, which can sometimes become an annoyance when you are in the middle of a fight, but some of the dialogue is quite funny so you can sort of take it with a pinch of salt there.
Impire gives the impression that it is a hard game, but in reality, you really have to be bad at the game to fail. The only way you lose a mission is if one of your treasure rooms is destroyed; I never saw it get destroyed once in my entire time playing this game.  Playing the game on the hardest difficulty may make it more of a challenge, rather than a grind; but I would of thought the medium setting would have given some sort of challenge.
So far I have put about sixty three hours into Impire – the story mode is split into five chapters, each has about five or six missions to them; you can sometimes spend an hour on each level,  this game has a serious amount of content to offer. Not to mention the multiplayer mode (something which I didn’t experience so will not comment on).
I did have one technical problem whilst playing the game – it can be played on all resolutions up to 4k which is nice to see; however even on the lower resolutions, you will notice quite a bit of stuttering on the cut scenes when the camera angel changes, it just looks janky but if you can ignore that you’ll be fine.  The game has a wide variety of graphical options so you can customize the graphics to match your rig very easily.
In summary; this is a brilliant Dungeon Builder game with a huge amount of content on offer. Fans of Dungeon Keeper should definitely be checking this game out.  The price of £14,99 may be considered high for some, but given how many hours I have put into this game, I am going to highly  recommend it.

I 1st played this straight after relase back in 2013, back then it was a buggy mess with some game breaking bugs that stopped the campaign advancing on certain missions and prevented one from playing multiplayer for more than a few minutes before desyncing for various reasons. A lot has improved since then and now in 2015 its much more stable and quite playable.
There are still bugs apparent, but they are generally minor.
Some of the more controversial game designs now come with a couple of different toggle settings ie ladders, fixed ladders and no ladders. Aggression can also be toggled in multiplayer and runes are now available to offset the other common gripe of keeping ones minions fed.
The largest problem with this game is still its UI and the way that so many simple things need user input in a needless but tedious manner, user micromanagement replaces the basic ai outside of combat (which the user has no control over).
Other gripes include disruptive and non immersive cutscenes that trigger throughout the levels pulling one away from their current set of actions. A clunky corridor and room placement design which offers no second chances even in the design phase of placement. A drop in Co-op that only saves the Hosts progression and offers only a partial co-op experience with players unable to share resources or enter each others domains in times of need making it feel more like single player with mutual objectives. And a mutiplayer aspect that is relaint upon pvp modes (in a very quiet community) with no ai or bots. (Edit: Our experience of the only co-op MP mode Survival was flawed by all but one player being bugged and stuck in their own dungeons, unable to access the global area even after the peace countdown had expired.)

Wow. Like, damn - what a game.
I mean this with all sincerity: props goes to Hello Games.
I've really wanted this game ever since E3 2014 when the trailer released. Now, obviously, the game did not live up to many's expectations, however I was still optimistic. I didn't end up buying the game when it launched - due to the initial reviews (and ever since Arkham Knight's launch I know not to) - but I've been watching and waiting ever since, reading reviews and following the development and patch notes.
It wasn't until August 11th that I saw the patch notes for 1.3. I saw all the new features and content that I had been looking for in a space adventure game for many years.
And I must say - after finally buying the game, almost exactly one year after launch - this game is a true work of art.
Not only is it packed full of content (with even more said to be one the way) and a blast to play, but visually, this game is, in my opinion, a master work of art. I can't even begin to describe what I've seen and experience in this game. Even just little things like the waves in the swaying grass from the wind and the sound effects of tree leaves rustling in the breeze - it amazed me at how much a video game made me smile just from pure awe.
Now, when I first got the game, I made sure to reserve all judgement until after about 4 or 5 hours, as thats when I heard many people saying it got boring and repetative. But, next thing I know I am past the 30 hour mark as of writing this, and I can say that I absolutly love this game.
tl;dr
If you love space, exploration, discovering new things, space battles, and along the way learning tons of lore, then this game is for you.
If you like the idea of a single player experience set within a universe shared by all player - then this game is for you.
8/10
P.S.
I was really excited when I went to the player-made database of places and regions of space other players have discovered in the game, only to find that the star cluster I had spawned in was not even listed as a discoverd region. The idea that everything I was seeing and experienceing in this part of this galaxy in this part of the universe had never been charted - let along discovered - by any other player really excited me and made excited to back into the game and see it all.

It's finally the game we all wanted.. Version 1.3 is everything the original release was supposed to be and more.
I have to say, I'm very impressed with Hello Games and it's commitment to a game a lot of people frankly wrote off. They've stayed the course, listen to it's fan base that never left and made huge strides to make the came reach it's potential. I've logged literally thousands of hours into RPG/Simulator/Adventure games and know what real grinding is. No Man's Sky makes it all worth it. The story and freedom is unique in such a way it's hard to stray from a particular sense of wanting to know the unknown. I'd start to focus on character building for a little while but then drop everything and chase the Path of Atlas. No matter how many times I stray from the storyline, I find myself falling back on track. Such a strange pull for such a limitless open world game. Anyway, the game is an absolutle must for anyone that showed interest from the start. Plus, it's on sale! Absolutely perfect time to buy this revolutionary game. I'm excited to see what else they cook up next.
Pros-
Unique Story Telling
Beautiful Game Play
Well Thought Out Controls
Creative Use of Scientific Theories
Consistant Updates/New Material
Dynamic/Unique Music
Complex Economic System
Cons-
Grind Is REAL (Yet Enjoyable) (Kind Of) (Give Me Credits Please)
Long Term Commitment Required (If Chasing Story/Upgrades/Tech) (Creative Mode Avaliable)
Nearly Zero Chance Of EVER Seeing Another Player
Requires A Pretty Beefy Computer To Run On Highest Settings (No Surprise)
Game was underwhelming at launch but now it's amazing and I find it awfully addicting. Definitely recommend it if you're into uniqueness and sci-fi!

To the Moon... is not really a game. I strongly recommend it though because the needs to be experienced to be believed. It'll make you laugh, smile, and cry, probably all at once. And I'll admit without shame that I bawled like a baby when the game was finished.
The very concept is weird even when explained to you in game, but it follows to scientists who barely get along on a routine job of granting a dying man's wish through memory rewriting. Again, it is not a game, and even plays with the concept with a joke battle against a "squirellmon"(?) that leaves a few kids shaming you for even attempting to hurt the little rodent. It's moments like these that play more like a kinetic novel that can give us funny moments, as well as sad and happy ones.
The game really picks up in the second and third acts, when it becomes less of a routine job and you are actually prevented from clearing your job. It would be spoilery to explain any further than that, and trust me when I say you're better going into this game blind. It is full of emotional impact and I myself broke into tears by the time the credits started to roll. To the Moon is short, but at $10 it is worth every cent even if you don't buy it on sale.
And if you can, pick up their soundtrack. Not only the music is beautiful, but half the money goes to charities towards autism.

is an excellent Historic-Science Fiction Action/Adventure Game mainly inspired by the novel Alamut written by Vladimir Bartol way back in 1938. The Game introduced many brilliant concepts and a totally different mindblowing plot which is very well connected from past to the present and you can devise many theories based on it. It was turned down by many people because it lacked variety and yes it did. I'm gonna list out the positive points between this game and its successors and also the reason why I think it's still an awesome game of the franchise. It had a special charm that none of it's successors had and will ever have.
The Game is simple and doesn't involve customisation or anything and doesn't feature money,etc to buy stuff and stays true in assassinating your targets. Whereas the other games got deviated into buying stuff and oh god the renovation business started.
Had some great concepts such as synchronisation for example, its not actually health but how close you (Desmond) could faithfully recreate the actions of ancestor, like if you carelessly fell off from a building or punched some civvy, etc. you lose the synchronisation, because the ancestor didn't do such thing in his life and was careful. It will regain over time and become stable when it is lost.
Where as in other games you have health and armor and the way to replenish it is to drink some health tonic. Death in all these games is actually just a bad sync-up where you replayed the ancestor's memory event so bad that you lost touch with the original one's completely, so the Animus reinitialises back to the point where it made sense before you screwed it up entirely.
So basically Ezio, etc. actually dies when you run out of it. Checkpoint restart is just a game mechanic. You can say that the Animus is still re-initialising the scene, but you died from lack of health, not loss of synchronization, So the Synchronisation no longer makes sense, so technically it was very well implemented and made some real actual sense in this game. And there are some other concepts which were not only solid and made sense but also gave a definite depth to the game.
It has darker and gritty atmosphere with well suited background scores as you scour for information about the target in various ways which gives you this 'Assassin' feeling. While the other games had peaceful and relaxing score not stating that they're bad but this one had better and showed how dark and unsafe the world is and was perfect for its Middle-Eastern setting.
The Chase Theme (Access the Animus as per OST) of this game is just goddamn EPIC.
"You are not a bloodthirsty berserker, nor an invincible warrior cutting through waves of guards - you are a blade in a crowd, someone, who doesn't exist...until the blade has pierced your targets throat. As the bells echo throughout the city and the guards draw their swords against you, you realize it is time to run...run and become no one once more.
The one thing that the original Assassin's Creed did better than ALL other sequels (everything up to Syndicate) is making you realize when it's time to run.﻿"

Hob is a must play game. It's a well crafted masterpiece in my opinion that needs your attention. Even if platforming and solving puzzles isn't your thing, the game is also an exploration-heavy action adventure, you will not be disappointed, you will love this.
Story:
You arrive in a new land, nobody there speaks your language, there is no text to help you, you don't know what you have to do but there seems to be a friendly robot that cares to guide you but never holds your hand,  you must figure things out by yourself. The lore of the game will "blow your mind" if you can find all the clues and once again i'll say that the game has zero text or speach that will tell you the lore, the way they tell you the story is brilliant.
Gameplay:
You solve puzzles, you complete challenging platforming levels you fight various of enemies and you collect stuff you find along the way to upgrade your character. Everything is requiring exloring and if you do it right you will find some very well hiden secrets. There is a rewarding feeling when you figure those puzzles out, and when you finally complete a cave/dungeon or kill a badas enemy with your minimal gear. The level design is perfect, i can't remember an other game with such a perfect level design.
Visuals:
This is a goreous game, everything is beautiful and very carefully placed in the world. There are some spots on the map that you will stop just to take some screenshots and admire the scenery or look for places you haven't been, even in lower end pc's the scenery and the backgrounds are beautiful.
Audio/Music:
Nobody speaks your language, but you can understand what the locals want to say to you, the music is very relaxing and the ambiance sounds help you to understand your surroundings.
Duration:
The game is "short", about 10-20 hours to reach the end, it took me 25-30 to uncover everything on the map. I don't say its not value for money, this game has so much to give to you. Nevertheless i wanted more of it, really badly. This game should be a series one day and Runic showed us in the past that they can do it.
Backtracking:
I was a bit confused in the beginning i had no idea what i was collecing or where i should go next. Later on i got used to it, everything made sense and i knew what i was looking for in each new area. I can see people getting lost for their first 20ish-30 minutes and backtrack a lot until they find out how to progress from the first areas but it's something that makes sense a bit later. Minor-spoiler if you are backtracking or lost: You can fast traver and look at your map!
Synopsis:
They worked really hard on this game and it something you can tell just from the first couple of minutes playing it or just watching a trailer. It's a game you must play by yourself and don't get spoiled by videos or streams, it's a game you must take your time to admire and don't rush to see the ending. The progression, the character upgrates, the new stuff they planned for each new area that the player was supposed to be, they crafted this game with love and passion. New mechanics, new jumps, new puzzles, new secrets, new everything in every corner. I loved the part that you could stop in most places to admire the scenery and to look for new places you haven't been and maybe take one screenshot or ten. I loved fighing bosses especially when i speedruned it with the bare essential gear as one of the achievements suggests. And i loved spending some time to understand the lore after i finished my first run and had no clue what happend.
Now it's your chance, make it home.

The quick and dirty recommendation guide (pick as many +/- points as you like and make up your mind if it's worth buying):
+ strong narrative
+ outstanding sound and visual presentation
+ responsive, intense and simple combat
+ nightmarish horror atmosphere (without jump scares)
+ superb voice acting
+ frightening and well-designed end bosses
+/- combat lacks complexity and may be too simple for some
+/- no replay value (it may have for a revisited experience)
+/- bit short, which is compensated by fair price and gameplay without tedious and lengthy grinds
+/- high stylized presentation of events and plot may not be everyone's taste (totally mine, though)
- gameplay doesn't offer much variety
- not much to explore apart from lore stones telling you about Norse mythology (which is quite important, however!)
- lack of variety in enemies and their appearance
The details:
Hellblade tells a story about suffering, sacrifice, darkness and endeavor. Following the story of Picts warrior maid Senua, you embark on a nightmarish and mind-twisting journey to Helheim, to save a beloved one’s soul. However, for Senua, many things aren’t what they’re supposed to be, for she’s suffering from severe psychosis. While you often can’t decide what’s real and what not, you must overcome many obstacles and enemies – the latter seemingly coming right out of Hel(l).
No other game, up to this point, managed to devour me – getting me so immersed – like Hellblade did. This game just pulled me deeper than any other game has accomplished in recent years, and I, mentally, switched off everything else around me and Senua’s reality became mine. The sound design and visual presentation is outstanding.
I was always a fan of non-linear storytelling and Hellblade totally nailed it. Its presentation is intriguing, captivating and keep you ever so interested in what happened (to Senua) and how everything will turn out.
As for the gameplay I was kind of surprised of what they came up with: There's a level where there is nothing but darkness and you have to find your way out, without fighting, only using your senses, as Senua's reaching out with her hand to frisk her surroundings, or running from one light source to another to not getting devoured by darkness. In other parts, cynically spoken, you could call it 'walking simulator', but, as for myself, I was so immersed in the world that I didn't mind. It doesn’t deliver any boredom even when ‘nothing’ happens.
There is one thing to explore off the main paths, however: Lore stones. These stones – telling you about Norse mythology in appearance of an old friend – are optional but critical in further expanding on the whole game’s story. At first one might not see the entangled meaning of Norse mythology and it seems rather random, just to give this game a Norse touch although you're not playing a viking heroine. Certainly, Vikings are involved in the story but that doesn’t necessarily explain why you keep hearing stories about the Northmen. But keep your wits about you and you’ll come to realize the importance of those stories.
I also enjoyed the combat, although it lacks complexity and deep mechanics. So, what is to like about it? Its responsiveness and simplicity made it a blast to play. It is quick, brutal, intense and it just works without any clumsiness. In that regard it is sort of 'flawless', straight on point. Don't expect anything near like Dark Souls, though.
Visual clues were used in a clever way and weren't spelled out boldly for you with exclamation marks, compass needles and the like. Even in one given situation where acting under pressure and time limit was required, I managed to find all the necessary clues at the first try without said compass needle or other HUD markers pointing out where to go – there are voices telling you to "focus" or to look in another direction. The lack of (almost) any meta information fits the theme of the game and it is an enjoyable change in a video game. That being said, there's no "meta game" telling you how to do things (apart from the game options menu). No HUD, no text boxes or pop ups. Everything you need to know to beat the game is offered by the environments and from 'within' the game.
It absolutely has become one of my favorite games by now.

The main complaint I have about this game is that it's just way too easy. I played on Extreme difficulty and I could still get through most of the levels without even taking damage.
The Dash move, which is unlocked at the start is basically just a sprint which makes you run at about 3 times the speed of sound. After each level you can buy upgrades which cost about half as much as a ♥♥♥♥ing Twix, and after upgrading the Dash a few times you can dash for about 30 seconds with a 3 second cooldown afterwards.
While dashing, you can walk on water, toxin and lava don't hurt you and you move too fast for enemy projectiles to be able to hit you. The only times you even need to bother with killing enemies are the levels where the objective is to clear out the area. When the objective is just to heal the tree at the end, or to collect all of the energy orbs, you can just sprint past the Flanx (enemies) and finish the level in about 30 seconds.
For attacks, the only one you need is the Pulse, which is basically a rocketlauncer that you can charge to do more damage, but just spamming the uncharged attack is enough to kill most enemies in no time once you've upgraded the attack a few times. Even the big♥♥♥♥♥bosses are a piece of cake once you know how to spam the attack.
The controls are good, and I like how your attacks can affect the level (shooting rockets makes craters appear etc.), and the monster design is pretty good and creative as well.
That said, the difficulty is really a dealbreaker and therefore I can't say I recommend Caster.
